definition_zh: 争端；质疑
definition_en: a serious disagreement, or to argue that something is not true
core_image: 两个人隔着一张桌子，各按着同一张纸的一角
scene: 两个人隔着一张桌子，各自按住同一张纸的一角。 The two families have been in dispute for years.
sceneCN: 这里 dispute 指「争端」（第 1 个义项：长期未决的争执）；句意是这两家已经争了多年。

derivatives.zh: 有争议的
争论者
无可争议的

senses.title: A serious disagreement
senses.definition: a serious disagreement that lasts or becomes public
senses.definitionCN: 持续或公开的严重分歧
senses.example: The two families have been in dispute for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这两家已经争了多年。
senses.why: One sheet of paper, two hands, no shared edge.
senses.whyCN: 一张纸，两只手，找不到共同的一边。

senses.title: To argue that something is false
senses.definition: to say that something is not true or not right
senses.definitionCN: 声称某事不真实或不对
senses.example: He disputed the amount on the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 他质疑账单上的金额。
senses.why: To dispute is to hold the paper and pull.
senses.whyCN: 质疑，就是按住那张纸往回拉。

intro.en: Dispute comes from Latin disputare, to argue a question, from dis- and putare, to think or reckon.
intro.cn: dispute 来自拉丁语 disputare（辩论一个问题），由 dis- 与 putare（思考、计算）构成。

items.en: Putare meant to think, to reckon or to prune.
items.cn: putare 指思考、计算，也指修剪。

items.en: Disputare meant to reckon a matter from both sides.
items.cn: disputare 指把事情两面都算一遍。

items.en: Disputer meant to argue or to quarrel.
items.cn: 古法语 disputer 指辩论或争吵。

items.en: English dispute named a formal argument.
items.cn: 英语 dispute 指正式的辩论。

items.en: It now also means to question a fact or a bill.
items.cn: 今天它也指对事实或账单提出质疑。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dispute stem, and the meaning group names other forms of conflict.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dispute 词干，近义组列出别的冲突形式。

entries.definition: open to argument
entries.definitionCN: 可以争辩的

entries.definition: a person who argues a case
entries.definitionCN: 争论某一方的人

entries.definition: argued about by others
entries.definitionCN: 被人争论的

entries.definition: a heated exchange of views
entries.definitionCN: 激烈的意见交锋

entries.definition: an angry disagreement between people
entries.definitionCN: 人与人之间带怒气的争执

entries.definition: a call to prove or defend something
entries.definitionCN: 要求证明或辩护的挑战

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with two hands on one sheet and end with a paper finally settled.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从两只手按住一张纸开始，落到一张终于说定的纸。

normal.en: Dis- plus pute: two sides reckon the same sum apart.
normal.cn: dis 加 pute，两方各算一遍同一笔账。

normal.en: A dispute over pay can stop a whole factory.
normal.cn: 薪酬上的争执，能让整座工厂停下。

normal.en: The land in dispute has no fence left standing.
normal.cn: 有争议的那块地，篱笆早没了。

normal.en: To dispute a bill is to ask for the sum again.
normal.cn: 质疑一张账单，就是要求再算一遍。

normal.en: An undisputed fact needs no loud voice.
normal.cn: 无可争议的事实，不需要大声。

abstract.en: Picture two hands pulling opposite corners.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手各拉一角。

abstract.en: Picture a torn edge between two people.
abstract.cn: 想象两人中间一道撕开的边。

abstract.en: Picture a third chair brought to the table.
abstract.cn: 想象桌边多搬来一把椅子。

examples.en: The two families have been in dispute for years.
examples.cn: 这两家已经争了多年。

examples.en: He disputed the amount on the bill.
examples.cn: 他质疑账单上的金额。

examples.en: The land is still in dispute between the villages.
examples.cn: 这块地仍在两村之间争执不下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dispute 记成「各算各的」：dis 是分开，put 与思考、计算同源；两个人分开各算一遍，算不到一处，就成了争端。

root: 源自拉丁语 disputare（辩论一个问题），由 dis-（分开）与 putare（思考、计算、修剪）构成，经古法语 disputer 进入英语。本义是两方各自把账算一遍，因此既指争执本身，也指对某个说法提出质疑。

sensesIntro.en: From two separate reckonings of one sum to the argument that follows.
sensesIntro.cn: 从对同一笔账的两次计算，到随之而来的争执。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands on opposite corners of one sheet of paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手按着同一张纸相对的两角。

branches.en: The first sense is the long disagreement itself.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是那场长期的分歧。

branches.en: The second sense is the act of pulling at one fact.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是对某个事实的拉扯。

branches.en: Both senses need at least two sides.
branches.cn: 两个义项都至少需要两方。

branches.en: Both can end when someone reads the paper again.
branches.cn: 两个义项都可能在有人重读那张纸时结束。

branches.en: Only the second sense can be done by one person alone.
branches.cn: 只有第二个义项能由一个人单独完成。

intro.en: Dispute belongs to the Latin putare family, where thinking, reckoning and arguing share a stem.
intro.cn: dispute 属于拉丁语 putare 一族，思考、计算与争辩共用同一词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin putare, to reckon, gives disputare and dispute, with dis- marking two separate reckonings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 putare（计算）给出 disputare 与 dispute，前缀 dis- 标出两次分开的计算。

items.example: They dispute the price every year.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年都为价格争执。
有争议的边界仍然关闭。

items.example: Two clerks stood disputing the sum.
items.exampleCN: 两名职员站着争那笔钱。

items.example: A disputatious mind enjoys a quarrel.
items.exampleCN: 爱争辩的头脑喜欢争吵。

definition_zh: 咬；咬伤；一口；刺痛
definition_en: to cut or crush something with your teeth
core_image: 咬下一口苹果留下的牙印
scene: 他对着红苹果咬下去，汁水顺着手腕流。 He took a bite and smiled.
sceneCN: 这里 bite 是「一口」（第 2 个义项：一次咬下的量）；句意是他咬了一口，然后笑了。

derivatives.zh: 刺骨的，形容风或寒冷锐利逼人
咬人的动物，也用于 nail biter 这类说法

senses.title: To cut with the teeth
senses.definition: to use the teeth to cut into something
senses.definitionCN: 用牙齿切入某物
senses.example: The dog bit the postman.
senses.exampleCN: 那条狗咬了邮递员。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, naming the action of the teeth.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，直接指牙齿的动作。

senses.title: An amount taken in one bite
senses.definition: the amount of food taken into the mouth at one time
senses.definitionCN: 一次送入口中的食物量
senses.example: She took a bite and smiled.
senses.exampleCN: 她咬了一口，笑了。
senses.why: The action became a noun for the amount it produces.
senses.whyCN: 动作转成名词，指这一次动作取下的量。

senses.title: A sharp stinging feeling
senses.definition: a sharp cold or painful feeling
senses.definitionCN: 尖锐的寒冷或疼痛感
senses.example: The wind had a real bite this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 今早的风真有些刺骨。
senses.why: Cold that seemed to cut the skin was pictured as teeth biting.
senses.whyCN: 像要割破皮肤的寒冷，被想象成牙齿在咬。

intro.en: Bite is an Old English strong verb whose past forms bit and bitten survived.
intro.cn: bite 是古英语的强变化动词，过去式 bit 与过去分词 bitten 沿用至今。

items.en: bitan meant to cut with the teeth.
items.cn: bitan 意为用牙齿切咬。

items.en: the past tense bit and participle bitten settled.
items.cn: 过去式 bit 与过去分词 bitten 固定下来。

items.en: bite also named a wound made by teeth.
items.cn: bite 也开始指牙齿造成的伤口。

items.en: writers used bite for sharp cold.
items.cn: 作家们用 bite 形容刺骨的寒冷。

items.en: bite keeps both the action and the amount senses.
items.cn: 如今 bite 兼指咬的动作与咬下的量。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the b-t pattern; the near-meaning group names other ways of using teeth.
note.cn: 形近组共用 b-t 的字母骨架；近义组是其他用牙的动作。

entries.definition: food used to attract fish

entries.definitionCN: 小口小口地咬

definition_zh: 味道；风味；调味
definition_en: the taste of food or drink, a distinctive quality, or to give food a particular taste
core_image: 一勺热汤在舌尖散开，先咸后鲜
scene: 这汤有淡淡的蒜味。 The soup has a light flavour of garlic.
sceneCN: 这里 flavour 是「味道」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这汤有淡淡的蒜味。

derivatives.zh: 调味品
无味的
风味浓郁的

senses.title: Taste
senses.definition: the taste that food or drink has in the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 食物或饮料在口中的味道
senses.example: The soup has a light flavour of garlic.
senses.exampleCN: 这汤有淡淡的蒜味。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense used for food and drink.
senses.whyCN: 这是描述饮食时最日常的义项。

senses.title: Character
senses.definition: a distinctive quality or atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 某种独特的气质或氛围
senses.example: The old town keeps a flavour of the past.
senses.exampleCN: 老城保留着过去的风味。
senses.why: Taste became a metaphor for character.
senses.whyCN: 味道被隐喻为事物的特色。

senses.title: Kind
senses.definition: a particular kind of food with a certain taste
senses.definitionCN: 带有特定味道的一类食品
senses.example: They sell ten flavours of ice cream.
senses.exampleCN: 他们卖十种口味的冰淇淋。
senses.why: Each kind of ice cream is named by its taste.
senses.whyCN: 每种冰淇淋都按味道来命名。

senses.title: To season
senses.definition: to give food a particular taste
senses.definitionCN: 给食物增添特定味道
senses.example: She flavoured the sauce with lemon.
senses.exampleCN: 她用柠檬给酱汁调味。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb of adding taste.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为添加味道的动词。

intro.cn: flavour 源自古法语 flaor，可能出自拉丁语中表示气味或吹拂的词。

items.en: Flare meant to blow or breathe out.

items.en: Flaor meant smell or taste.

items.en: Flavour named the taste of food.

items.en: The word extended to atmosphere and character.

note.en: Flavour is compared with similar-looking words and with words for taste and smell.

normal.en: This tea has a floral flavour.

normal.en: Which flavour do you want?

normal.en: A flavour enhancer adds taste.

abstract.en: Taste is memory arriving through the tongue.
abstract.cn: 味道是经由舌头抵达的记忆。

abstract.en: A place has a flavour no menu can list.
abstract.cn: 一个地方的风味是菜单列不出的。

abstract.en: Small additions change the whole dish.
abstract.cn: 少许添加就能改变整道菜。

examples.en: She flavoured the sauce with lemon.
examples.cn: 她用柠檬给酱汁调味。

dict_mnemonic.text: flavour 经古法语 flaor 上溯到拉丁语 flare（吹），本义「随空气传来的气味」，后专指味道与风味。

branches.en: Taste and character share the same word.

intro.en: Flavour builds a small family of tastes, tools, and qualities.

definition_zh: 两次；两倍；双倍地
definition_en: two times, or double the amount or degree of something
core_image: 同一件事做了第二遍，或数量翻了一倍
scene: 闹钟没响，小李一个早晨已经迟到两回，工资单上还写着翻倍的加班时数。 He was late twice this morning and did not dare complain.
sceneCN: 这里 twice 是副词「两次」（第 1 个义项：做某事两回）；句意为今天早上他迟到了两次，工资单上加班时数也照两倍计。

derivatives.zh: 同源基数词，twice 即「两」的副词形式
同源序数词，义为「第十二」，与 two 同属古英语 twa 词族
同源数词，本义为「两个十」

senses.title: Two times, on two occasions
senses.definition: on two occasions or in two instances
senses.definitionCN: 在两个场合或发生两回
senses.example: I called her twice, but she did not answer.
senses.exampleCN: 我给她打了两次电话，她都没接。
senses.why: The core image is repetition counted to two: the same act laid out a second time.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是数到二的重复：同一个动作又铺开了一遍。

senses.title: Double the amount
senses.definition: double in quantity, size, degree or amount
senses.definitionCN: 数量、尺寸、程度或金额上的加倍
senses.example: This room is twice as large as the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间比旧的那间大一倍。
senses.why: Counting occasions becomes counting quantity: two units of the same measure stacked together.
senses.whyCN: 计次的「两回」变成计量的「两份」：同样的度量单位叠加了两次。

senses.title: Twice over: again a second time
senses.definition: in the phrase twice over, done a second time in addition to the first
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 twice over，指在第一次之外再做第二遍
senses.example: He checked the figures twice over before signing.
senses.exampleCN: 签字前他把数字核了两遍。
senses.why: The phrase makes the repetition explicit: the act is performed, then performed again.
senses.whyCN: 短语把重复显性化：动作做完之后再来一遍。

senses.title: Think twice: hesitate before acting
senses.definition: in the phrase think twice, to consider carefully before deciding or acting
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 think twice，指决定或行动前慎重考虑
senses.example: You should think twice before lending money to a stranger.
senses.exampleCN: 借钱给陌生人之前你该三思。
senses.why: The mind runs over the matter a second time; the second pass is the caution.
senses.whyCN: 头脑把事情再过一遍；这第二次过就是审慎。

senses.title: Twice removed: two steps in kinship
senses.definition: in phrases like first cousin twice removed, separated by two generations
senses.definitionCN: 用于 first cousin twice removed 等短语，指亲属关系相隔两代
senses.example: She is my cousin twice removed on my mother's side.
senses.exampleCN: 她是我母亲那边隔两代的表亲。
senses.why: Kinship is measured in steps, and twice counts two steps down the ladder.
senses.whyCN: 亲属关系按代步计，twice 数出往下隔的两代。

senses.title: Lightning never strikes twice: rarity of repetition
senses.definition: in the saying lightning never strikes twice, an unlucky event is unlikely to happen again in the same place
senses.definitionCN: 谚语 lightning never strikes twice，指倒霉的事不大可能在同一处重演
senses.example: After losing two wallets, he joked that lightning never strikes twice.
senses.exampleCN: 连丢两个钱包后，他自嘲说祸不单行这种事不会再来一次。
senses.why: The proverb plays on the counting: one strike is bad luck, a second strike would be twice.
senses.whyCN: 谚语玩的是计数：一次倒霉是运气差，再来一次才算「两次」。

senses.title: Twice told: repeated words
senses.definition: in literary use, twice told describes a story or remark that has been told before and is told again
senses.definitionCN: 文学用法，twice told 形容已讲过又再讲的故事或话
senses.example: He opened the meeting with a twice told tale about the founding of the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 他以一个讲过多次的公司创业老故事开场。
senses.why: The count attaches to the telling: the tale has now completed its second round.
senses.whyCN: 计数落在「讲」上：故事如今完成了第二轮。

senses.title: Twice as much again: compounding increase
senses.definition: in the phrase twice as much again, an increase equal to the original amount on top of it
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 twice as much again，指在原有数量之上再增加与原量相等的部分
senses.example: The new plant can turn out twice as much again as the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 新厂的产量能在旧厂的基础上再翻一倍。
senses.why: The doubling is measured against the base: what exists once is matched by an equal second amount.
senses.whyCN: 加倍以原有数量为基准：已有的一份再配上等量的第二份。

intro.en: Twice is the old adverb of two, built inside English on a native numeral root.
intro.cn: twice 是 two 的古式副词，在英语内部由本族数词词根构成。

items.en: *dwo- is generally reconstructed as the numeral 'two'; its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *dwo- 是数词「二」；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Proto-Germanic gave *twai, the ancestor of English two, and a related doubling form *twiz-
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语给出 *twai，即英语 two 的祖先，另有一个相关的叠倍形式 *twiz-。

items.en: Old English had twige, twiwa 'two times, doubly', built directly on the numeral twā 'two'.
items.cn: 古英语有 twige、twiwa，义为「两次、加倍」，直接建立在数词 twā「二」之上。

items.en: Middle English twies added the adverbial -s, like the ending in once and besides.
items.cn: 中古英语 twies 加上了副词性词尾 -s，与 once、besides 的词尾相同。

items.en: The spelling twice settled by the fourteenth century, and the double-quantity sense was already common.
items.cn: 十四世纪拼写定型为 twice，「两倍」义当时已很常用。

items.en: Fixed phrases such as think twice and twice removed keep the word busy far beyond plain counting.
items.cn: think twice、twice removed 等固定短语让这个词的用法远远超出单纯的计数。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the numeral family and the adverbial -s twins; the near-meaning group gathers words of repetition and doubling.
note.cn: 形近组收数词词族与同词尾副词；近义组收表重复与加倍的词。

entries.definition: One time; built on the numeral one with the same adverbial ending.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「一次」，由数词 one 加同样的副词词尾构成。

entries.definition: Three times; the old parallel adverb of three, now literary.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「三次」，three 的古式对应副词，今多用于文学。

entries.definition: To wind two strands together or to turn; looks and sounds close but is a different verb with a different history.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「捻合；拧转」，音形与 twice 相近，但是另一个动词，词源不同。

entries.definition: One of two children born together; from the same doubling numeral root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「双胞胎之一」，出自同一个表示「成双」的数词词根。

entries.definition: The ordinal of twelve; from the numeral family that also produced twice.
entries.definitionCN: 序数词，义为「第十二」，出自同样产出 twice 的数词词族。

entries.definition: Twice as much, or to make something twice as much; the adjective and verb counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或动词，义为「两倍的；使加倍」，与 twice 的「两倍」义互为表里。

entries.definition: One more time; marks a single repetition rather than the count of two.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「再次」，标记单次重复，而非「两次」这一计数。

entries.definition: Many times over; the count is left open instead of fixed at two.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「反复地」，次数开放不定，而非固定为两次。

entries.definition: To twice the degree; formal counterpart of the doubling sense.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「加倍地」，是「两倍」义的正式对应词。

entries.definition: Coming after the first; names the position that a second occurrence takes.
entries.definitionCN: 序数词，义为「第二」，标出第二次发生所处的位置。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real numeral root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的数词词根，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Twice is two with an adverbial s, exactly like once from one.
normal.cn: twice 就是 two 加副词词尾 s，与 once 之于 one 完全平行。

normal.en: Twice a week is a rhythm: Monday and Thursday, two beats.
normal.cn: twice a week 是一种节奏：周一和周四，两拍。

normal.en: Think twice means run the thought through your head two times.
normal.cn: think twice 意为让这个念头在脑中过两遍。

normal.en: Twice as much is two copies of the same amount stacked up.
normal.cn: twice as much 就是把同样的量叠上两份。

normal.en: Thrice is its triplet brother: once, twice, thrice.
normal.cn: thrice 是它的三胞胎兄弟：once、twice、thrice。

abstract.en: Picture one footprint, then a second one landing exactly on top of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个脚印，接着第二个脚印不偏不倚落在上面。

abstract.en: A doubled dose is the same cup poured into the glass a second time.
abstract.cn: 加倍就是把同一杯又倒了一遍。

abstract.en: Caution is the second pass of the mind over the same road.
abstract.cn: 审慎就是让头脑在同一条路上再走第二遍。

examples.en: The museum opens twice a week for school groups.
examples.cn: 博物馆每周为学校团体开放两次。

examples.en: Our new office is twice the size of the old one.
examples.cn: 我们的新办公室是旧办公室的两倍大。

examples.en: Read the contract twice before you put your name on it.
examples.cn: 签字之前把合同读两遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「太吾事」——两遍都太吾事没做好：两次、两倍

root: 古英语 twige「两次」直接建立在数词 twā「二」之上，经中古英语 twies 加副词性 -s 演变为 twice；数词本身来自原始日耳曼语 *twai，可追溯至原始印欧语 *dwo-（重构形式），与 two、twin、twelve、twenty 同族。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of twice all count to two: repeated occasions, doubled amounts, a second telling, the second pass of caution, kinship steps, proverbs, and compounded increases.
sensesIntro.cn: twice 的八个义项都数到二：重复的场合、加倍的量、第二次的讲述、审慎的第二遍过、亲等的两步、谚语，以及叠加式增长。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same act or amount is laid down a second time.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一个动作或数量被第二次放下。

branches.en: THE REPEATED ACT: two occasions, a second telling, a tale told twice over.
branches.cn: 重复动作线：两个场合、第二次讲述、讲了第二遍的故事。

branches.en: THE DOUBLED AMOUNT: two stacked measures, and a further increase on top of them.
branches.cn: 加倍数量线：两份叠加的量，以及在其之上的再增长。

branches.en: THE CAUTIOUS MIND: the thought runs a second time before the feet move.
branches.cn: 审慎心智线：脚未动，念头先再过一遍。

branches.en: THE FAMILY TREE: two generations down the kinship ladder.
branches.cn: 家族谱系线：亲等梯子往下的两代。

branches.en: THE PROVERB: one strike is misfortune, a second would be twice.
branches.cn: 谚语线：一次是倒霉，再来一次才算「两次」。

intro.en: Twice is a single native numeral adverb, but its family of tw- words is large and old.
intro.cn: twice 是单个的本族数词副词，但其 tw- 词族既庞大又古老。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, not Latin, so there are no Latin cognates to list; the Indo-European root is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语源而非拉丁语源，故没有拉丁同族词可列；印欧词根属重构形式。

items.example: The numeral is the base of the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 这个数词是该副词的基础。

items.meaning: forms adverbs of manner or number
items.meaningCN: 构成方式或数目的副词
items.example: It also appears in once and besides.
items.exampleCN: 同样的词尾也见于 once 与 besides。

items.example: It appears in twilight, the half-light of two states.
items.exampleCN: 它见于 twilight，即两种状态之间的微光。

items.example: The reconstructed root lies behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个重构词根是整个词族的源头。

items.example: It carries the same meaning from Latin, via duplex.
items.exampleCN: 它经 duplex 从拉丁语带来同样的「两倍」义。
它构成 bicycle 与 biannual。

items.example: It names the position of the second occurrence.
items.exampleCN: 它标出第二次发生的位置。

derivatives.zh: 同源基数词，义为「二」，twice 的数词基础
同源序数词，义为「第十二」
同源数词，本义「两个十」

definition_zh: 反对；异议；反对的理由；不赞成
definition_en: the act of saying that you disagree with something, the reason you give for that disagreement, or a formal protest made in a legal process
core_image: 掌心朝前抬起的一只手，把正在推进的事按住
scene: 庭审进行到一半，辩护律师从座位上站起，手里还捏着那页写满批注的证词。 The defence lawyer raised an objection before the witness could answer.
sceneCN: 这里 objection 是「正式异议」（第 3 个义项：法律程序中提出的反对）；句意为辩护律师在证人开口之前提出了异议。图中可辨识物件：法庭座位、批注过的证词、抬起的手。

pos.zh: 反对；异议；反对的理由；不赞成

derivatives.zh: objection 的基础词，作动词义为「反对」，作名词义为「物体」
由 object 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -or 构成，义为「反对者」
由 objection 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「令人反感的；可反对的」

senses.title: The act of saying you disagree
senses.definition: the act of expressing disagreement with a plan, an idea or a statement
senses.definitionCN: 对计划、想法或说法表示不赞同的举动
senses.example: Her objection was quiet but it stopped the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 她的反对很轻，却让表决停了下来。
senses.why: Latin objectio names the act of throwing something against, so the word starts with a gesture of resistance rather than with a reason.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 objectio 指「把东西对着扔过去」的动作，所以这个词的起点是抵抗的姿态，而不是一条理由。

senses.title: A reason given for disagreeing
senses.definition: a reason or argument that someone gives to show why something should not be done
senses.definitionCN: 某人给出的、说明为什么不该做某事的理由或论据
senses.example: The main objection was the cost of the new bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 主要的反对理由是这座新桥的造价。
senses.why: A protest thrown at a plan has to carry something with it, and the reason becomes the thing thrown, so the act and its argument come to share one word.
senses.whyCN: 扔向计划的抗议总得带上点东西，那条理由就是被扔出去的东西，于是动作与理由共用了一个词。

senses.title: A formal protest in a legal process
senses.titleCN: 正式异议；法律上的异议
senses.definition: a formal statement of disapproval made during a trial, a hearing or an official procedure
senses.definitionCN: 在庭审、听证或官方程序中正式提出的不赞成
senses.example: The judge overruled the objection and let the witness continue.
senses.exampleCN: 法官驳回异议，让证人继续说下去。
senses.why: In court the gesture is written into procedure, so objectio becomes a fixed move that a lawyer is allowed to make at a set moment.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上，这个姿态被写进了程序，objectio 于是变成律师可以在特定时刻做出的一个固定动作。

intro.en: Objection is the noun of action behind object: Latin threw something against, and the noun named both the throw and the thing thrown, which is why it can mean the protest and the reason for it.
intro.cn: objection 是 object 背后的动作名词：拉丁语「对着扔」，这个名词既指扔的动作，也指被扔出去的东西，所以它能同时表示抗议与抗议的理由。

items.en: Jacere, to throw, is the source of the -ject stem shared by object, objection and project.
items.cn: jacere 意为投掷，是 object、objection、project 共用的 -ject 词干的来源。

items.en: Obicere meant to throw something in front of someone, and in argument it meant to put a charge or a protest in another person's way.
items.cn: obicere 意为把东西抛到某人面前，在争论里指把一项指责或抗议挡到别人面前。

items.en: Objectio named the act of throwing against and also the words or grounds that were thrown, which is the exact double sense English keeps.
items.cn: objectio 既指「对着扔」的动作，也指被扔出的那些话与理由；英语保留的正是这双重的意思。

items.en: Old French objection carried the word into English law and debate, where a protest had to be stated in a set form.
items.cn: 古法语 objection 把这词带进英语的法律与辩论，那里提出抗议必须按既定格式陈述。

items.en: Modern English keeps the everyday sense of disagreeing, the sense of a stated reason, and the courtroom sense of a formal protest.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留三种用法：日常的不赞同、说明的理由，以及法庭上的正式异议。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the -ject stem and the family grown from object; the near-meaning group gathers words for complaint and resistance.
note.cn: 形近组沿 -ject 词干与 object 长出的词族；近义组收表示抱怨与抵制的词。

entries.definition: The noun for a thing, and the verb for disagreeing.
entries.definitionCN: 指物体的名词，也指表示反对的动词。

entries.definition: A person who formally opposes something.
entries.definitionCN: 正式反对某事的人；反对者。

entries.definition: Unpleasant, or open to being opposed.
entries.definitionCN: 令人不快或可被反对的。

entries.definition: An aim, or a judgement free of personal bias.
entries.definitionCN: 目标，或不受个人偏见影响的判断。

entries.definition: An object thrown through the air, such as a bullet.
entries.definitionCN: 被抛射出去的物体，如子弹。

entries.definition: A strong public statement that something is wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 公开而强烈地表示某事不对。

entries.definition: A statement that something is unsatisfactory.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事令人不满的说法。

entries.definition: Disagreement with an official opinion or decision.
entries.definitionCN: 对官方意见或决定的不赞同。

entries.definition: Resistance to a plan, a policy or a group.
entries.definitionCN: 对计划、政策或团体的抵制。

normalIntro.en: The word is the noun of action of object, so it holds both what a person does and what a person has to say.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 object 的动作名词，所以它既装着一个人做出的动作，也装着一个人要说的话。

normal.en: Objection is object plus -ion, and the suffix turns the act of throwing against into a thing that can be raised and answered.
normal.cn: objection 由 object 加 -ion 构成，后缀把「对着扔」的动作变成一个可以提出、也可以被回答的东西。

normal.en: Raise an objection is the standard pairing, because objections are imagined as something lifted up in a meeting.
normal.cn: raise an objection 是最常见的搭配，因为异议被想象成会议里被举起的东西。

normal.en: Have no objection means you do not oppose it, a phrase common in letters and agreements.
normal.cn: have no objection 意为不反对，是信件与协议里的常用说法。

normal.en: In court a lawyer says objection and the judge either sustains it or overrules it, two verbs that show how formal the move is.
normal.cn: 在法庭上律师说 objection，法官或者 sustain，或者 overrule；这两个动词显出这个动作有多正式。

normal.en: Objector is the person, objectionable is the quality, and object is both the thing and the act of disagreeing.
normal.cn: objector 是人，objectionable 是性质，object 既是物，也是出言反对。

abstract.en: An objection is a hand held up in front of a plan that is already moving.
abstract.cn: 异议就是在一件正在推进的事情前面举起的手。

abstract.en: Every objection carries two things at once: the refusal, and the reason that makes the refusal stand.
abstract.cn: 每一条异议都同时带着两样东西：拒绝，以及让拒绝站得住脚的理由。

abstract.en: A word that can be spoken both in a meeting and in a court shows how disagreement borrows procedure to gain weight.
abstract.cn: 一个既能在会议里说、也能在法庭上说的词，说明不赞同要借程序的形式来加分量。

examples.en: Her objection was quiet but it stopped the vote.
examples.cn: 她的反对很轻，却让表决停了下来。

examples.en: The main objection was the cost of the new bridge.
examples.cn: 主要的反对理由是这座新桥的造价。

examples.en: The judge overruled the objection and let the witness continue.
examples.cn: 法官驳回异议，让证人继续说下去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我不借，可申」——不想借就当面申明理由；objection 是反对与异议。

root: 由 object 加名词后缀 -ion 构成；object 一般认为来自拉丁语 objectum，源于 obicere（对着投掷），由 ob-（对着）加 jacere（投掷）构成，经古法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is refusal thrown at something; the senses divide into the act itself, the reason that supports it, and the formal shape it takes in court.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把拒绝扔向某件事；义项分成动作本身、支撑动作的理由，以及它在法庭上取得的正式形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a palm raised before something that is already moving forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：掌心朝前抬起的一只手，把正在推进的事按住。

branches.en: a quiet voice that stops a vote
branches.cn: 一句轻轻的反对让表决停下

branches.en: the cost of a bridge named as the reason
branches.cn: 把桥的造价说成理由

branches.en: a lawyer standing up in the middle of a question
branches.cn: 律师在提问中途站起来

branches.en: a refusal that only stands once a reason is attached
branches.cn: 只有接上理由才站得住的拒绝

branches.en: the same reason moved from talk into procedure
branches.cn: 同一条理由，从谈话搬进程序

intro.en: The word is a Latin noun of action built on the verb for throwing against, and its English endings give it a person, a quality and a base verb.
intro.cn: 这个词是建立在「对着投掷」动词上的拉丁动作名词，它的英语后缀又给出一个人、一种性质和基础动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin objectio, a throwing against, is the direct recorded ancestor of this noun, and it rests on obicere and jacere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 objectio（对着扔）是这个名词有记录的直系祖先，它立在 obicere 与 jacere 之上。

definition_zh: 肮脏的；污秽的；下流的；令人厌恶的；（天气）恶劣的
definition_en: covered with dirt; extremely dirty; obscene or disgusting; used to describe very bad weather
core_image: 一只摸过下水道口的手，黑泥嵌在指纹里怎么搓都搓不掉
scene: 维修工从污水井里爬上来，手套上糊满黑泥，他皱着眉说。 His gloves were filthy after he climbed out of the sewer.
sceneCN: 这里 filthy 是「肮脏的、沾满污垢的」（第 1 个义项：被脏东西覆盖）；句意是他从污水井爬出来后手套上全是污垢。

pos.zh: 肮脏的；污秽的；满是污垢的
下流的；猥亵的；道德败坏的
（口语）令人厌恶的；（天气）恶劣的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词性名词 filth 加形容词后缀 -y 构成 filthy；filth 本身义为「污物；秽语」
filthy 加名词后缀 -ness，义为「肮脏；污秽」
filthy 加副词后缀 -ly，义为「肮脏地；下流地」
与 filthy 同族的日耳曼源形容词，义为「难闻的；肮脏的」

senses.title: Covered with dirt
senses.definition: covered with or full of dirt and stains
senses.definitionCN: 被污垢、泥渍覆盖或沾满脏东西
senses.example: The floor was filthy after the dog ran through the mud.
senses.exampleCN: 狗踩过泥地之后，地板变得很脏。
senses.why: The word grew from filth, so the base picture is matter that clings to surfaces and refuses to come off.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从 filth（污物）长出来，核心画面是黏在表面上、怎么擦都擦不掉的脏东西。

senses.title: Extremely dirty in degree
senses.definition: so dirty that it shocks or disgusts people
senses.definitionCN: 脏到让人震惊或反感的程度
senses.example: The kitchen was filthy; even the cups had a layer of grease.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房脏得吓人，连杯子都蒙着一层油。
senses.why: Adding -y to filth intensifies it into an adjective of degree: not just dirty, but dirt itself made visible.
senses.whyCN: 在 filth 后加 -y 使之成为程度形容词：不只是「脏」，而是「污物本身显形」。

senses.title: Obscene or indecent
senses.definition: relating to sex in a rude or offensive way
senses.definitionCN: 以粗俗冒犯的方式涉及性，如低俗笑话或言语
senses.example: He told a filthy joke at dinner and everyone went silent.
senses.exampleCN: 他在晚饭时讲了个下流笑话，所有人都沉默了。
senses.why: Dirt applied to language: words treated as mental grime become obscene speech.
senses.whyCN: 把「脏」从物理挪到语言上：被视为心灵污垢的言语就成了下流话。

senses.title: Morally corrupt
senses.definition: morally bad or dishonest, especially for the sake of money
senses.definitionCN: 道德上恶劣或不诚实，尤指为钱财不择手段
senses.example: The novel describes a filthy merchant who cheats his own workers.
senses.exampleCN: 小说描写了一个欺压自己工人的卑鄙商人。
senses.why: Moral dirt is the metaphor: corruption of money and conduct is imagined as grime on the soul.
senses.whyCN: 这是「道德之脏」的隐喻：金钱与品行上的败坏被想象成灵魂上的污垢。

senses.title: Disgusting or unpleasant
senses.definition: very unpleasant, especially in taste, smell, or habit
senses.definitionCN: 非常令人不快，尤指气味、味道或习惯上的恶心
senses.example: The water in the bottle tasted filthy and warm.
senses.exampleCN: 瓶子里的水又温又恶心。
senses.why: Senses of touch, smell and taste share one channel with dirt, so disgust spills from one sense to all.
senses.whyCN: 触觉、嗅觉、味觉与「脏」共用同一通道，厌恶感由一个感官蔓延到全部。

senses.title: Bad weather
senses.definition: used about weather that is cold, wet and unpleasant
senses.definitionCN: 形容又冷又湿、令人难受的天气
senses.example: We stayed indoors all day because the weather was filthy.
senses.exampleCN: 天气恶劣，我们整天待在屋里。
senses.why: Rain and mud literally produce dirt, so foul weather is naturally called filthy.
senses.whyCN: 风雨泥泞确实会制造脏污，所以恶劣天气被顺理成章地称作 filthy。

senses.title: Extremely rich
senses.definition: informal, used in the phrase filthy rich about people with a great deal of money
senses.definitionCN: 口语用法，出现在 filthy rich 这一短语中，形容极有钱的人
senses.example: Her uncle is filthy rich but still drives an old car.
senses.exampleCN: 她叔叔富得流油，却仍开着一辆旧车。
senses.why: The older phrase filthy lucre linked money with moral dirt, and filthy rich keeps that ironic flavor.
senses.whyCN: 更早的 filthy lucre（不义之财）把金钱与道德之脏相连，filthy rich 保留了这种反讽味道。

senses.title: Overflowing or excessive
senses.definition: used about amounts of something unpleasant that are disgustingly large
senses.definitionCN: 形容令人反感的数量多到让人作呕
senses.example: Flies bred in the filthy heap of garbage behind the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 苍蝇在店后那堆脏乱得吓人的垃圾里滋生。
senses.why: When dirt accumulates beyond tolerance, the same adjective measures quantity as well as quality.
senses.whyCN: 当脏污积累到超出忍受范围，同一个形容词就从描述性质延伸到描述数量。

intro.en: Filthy is the adjective of filth, a native Germanic word, and its history is unusually clean to trace: foul to filth to filthy.
intro.cn: filthy 是 filth 的形容词形式，filth 是日耳曼本土词，其词源脉络异常清晰：foul → filth → filthy。

items.en: The reconstructed root *fulaz meant rotten, corrupt or dirty; it gave related forms across Germanic languages.
items.cn: 重构形式 *fulaz 意为「腐烂的、败坏的、脏的」，在各日耳曼语言中产生同族词形。

items.en: Old English had ful meaning foul, and formed the noun fulth, dirt or refuse, with an abstract noun suffix.
items.cn: 古英语有 ful（污秽的），并用抽象名词后缀构成 fulth，义为「污物、秽物」。

items.en: The noun became filth, and by the twelfth century the adjective filthi appeared, meaning covered with filth.
items.cn: 名词演变为 filth，约十二世纪出现形容词 filthi，意为「沾满污物的」。

items.en: The extended senses developed: obscene language, morally corrupt conduct, and foul weather are all recorded in this period.
items.cn: 引申义在此时期出现：下流言语、道德败坏的行径、恶劣天气均有文献记载。

items.en: Today filthy covers dirtiness of body and place, foul speech, disgusting taste, bad weather, and the ironic phrase filthy rich.
items.cn: 如今 filthy 覆盖身体与场所的脏、污秽言语、恶心的味道、恶劣天气，以及带反讽色彩的 filthy rich。

note.en: These neighbors share spelling roots or dirty-weather meanings, and it is easy to mix them up.
note.cn: 下列词与 filthy 在拼写、同根或「脏、恶劣」义场上相近，容易混淆。

entries.definitionCN: 污物、秽物或下流材料；filthy 的名词来源

entries.definition: smelling or tasting bad; against the rules; foul weather is stormy
entries.definitionCN: 难闻难吃的；犯规的；foul weather 指风雨天气；与 filthy 同出日耳曼词根，形容词义高度重叠

entries.definition: not clean; the plain everyday word for dirty things
entries.definitionCN: 不干净的；日常通用词，程度弱于 filthy

entries.definition: very unpleasant, disgusting, or spiteful
entries.definitionCN: 令人不快的；恶心的；恶毒的；强调主观厌恶感

entries.definition: extremely dirty and unpleasant, often about living conditions
entries.definitionCN: 肮脏悲惨的；多用于居住环境的整体脏乱，书面色彩更重

normalIntro.cn: 从词的组成入手：filth（污物）加形容词后缀。

normal.cn: filth + -y：污物的名词直接变成肮脏的形容词。

normal.cn: filthy 与 filth 保留了古英语词根 ful（污秽）演变来的 th。

normal.en: foul and filthy are cousins: foul smell, filthy smell, both Germanic.
normal.cn: foul 与 filthy 是同族：foul smell 与 filthy smell 都出自日耳曼词源。

normal.en: filthy rich is a fixed phrase: money imagined as moral grime.
normal.cn: filthy rich 是固定短语：把巨富想象成道德上的污垢。

normal.en: filthy weather = foul weather: rain that leaves mud on everything.
normal.cn: filthy weather 与 foul weather 同义：把一切都弄得泥泞的雨。

abstract.en: Picture a glove pulled out of a sewer: the grime has soaked through.
abstract.cn: 想象一只从污水井里捞出的手套：黑泥已浸透掌心。

abstract.en: Hear a joke that makes the whole table go silent.
abstract.cn: 听到一个让全桌人瞬间沉默的下流笑话。

abstract.en: Feel the disgust of warm water with grease floating on top.
abstract.cn: 体会一口浮着油花温水带来的恶心感。

examples.en: His gloves were filthy after he worked in the sewer all afternoon.
examples.cn: 他在下水道里干了一下午活后，手套脏得不成样子。

examples.en: Nobody wants to hear filthy jokes in the office.
examples.cn: 办公室里没人想听下流笑话。

examples.en: The weather turned filthy again, with cold rain and heavy fog.
examples.cn: 天气又变得恶劣起来，冷雨夹着浓雾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肥屍地」——满地都是肥腻的污垢，像地上爬满油泥一样脏，联想到 filthy 就是「脏透了」。

root: 古英语 ful（污秽的）加抽象名词后缀构成 fulth，即现代 filth（污物）；filth 再加形容词后缀 -y 得 filthy。与日耳曼同族词 foul（难闻的、肮脏的）同出一源；一般认为重构词根为 *fulaz。

sensesIntro.en: From literal dirt the word spreads to dirty language, dirty morals, disgusting tastes, foul weather, and finally ironic wealth.
sensesIntro.cn: 从字面的脏污出发，这个词蔓延到下流言语、败坏品行、恶心味道、恶劣天气，最后落到反讽的巨富。

branches.cn: 「脏」移入言语与道德：下流与卑鄙

branches.en: Disgust through taste, smell and habits

branches.en: Weather and accumulated filth as foulness

senses.exampleCN: 他把演讲的粗稿发给我。
senses.why: The word first meant something pulled or drawn out, so a draft is the part of a text pulled out from the mind before it sets.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早表示「被拉出来、画出来的东西」，所以草稿就是从脑子里先拉出来的那一部分文字，尚未定型。

senses.title: A plan not yet final
senses.definition: a written plan or proposal that still has to be discussed and approved
senses.definitionCN: 尚待讨论与批准的书面计划或提案
senses.example: The committee rejected the draft budget.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会否决了预算草案。
senses.why: A budget also starts as a drawn outline before it becomes binding, so the same word covers any unfinished plan.
senses.whyCN: 预算同样先有一个画出来的框架，之后才变得有约束力，因此同一个词也指任何未定案的计划。

senses.title: An order to pay money
senses.definition: a written order asking a bank to pay a sum of money to a named person
senses.definitionCN: 要求银行向指定的人支付一笔款项的书面指令
senses.example: The buyer paid by bank draft.
senses.exampleCN: 买家以银行汇票付款。
senses.why: A payment order is also a drawn writing, a document pulled out of an account, so banking borrowed the same word.
senses.whyCN: 付款指令也是一种「画出来的文书」，是从账户里拉出的一纸凭证，于是银行沿用了同一个词。

senses.title: A current of air in a room
senses.definition: a stream of cool air that comes through a window or a gap
senses.definitionCN: 从窗户或缝隙进来的冷气流
senses.example: A cold draft came under the door.
senses.exampleCN: 一股冷风从门底下钻进来。
senses.why: This sense is a separate English word for pulling, because air is literally drawn or pulled through a gap.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个英语词，本义是「拉、拖」，因为风正是被从缝隙里拉进来的。

senses.title: To write an early version
senses.definition: to write the first version of a letter, speech, or plan
senses.definitionCN: 写出信件、演讲或计划的第一个版本
senses.example: They asked her to draft the reply.
senses.exampleCN: 他们请她起草回信。
senses.why: Since a draft is the pulled-out version, the verb simply names the act of producing that version.
senses.whyCN: 既然草稿是「先拉出来的那一版」，动词自然就是「把那一版写出来」这个动作。

senses.title: To call people into military service
senses.definition: to order people to join the armed forces or to move staff to another job
senses.definitionCN: 命令人们入伍，或把人员调去别的岗位
senses.example: He was drafted into the army at nineteen.
senses.exampleCN: 他十九岁时被征召入伍。
senses.why: People are pulled out of ordinary life the way a plan is pulled out of the mind, so the same verb serves military service.
senses.whyCN: 人被从日常生活中「拉走」，正如计划从脑子里被拉出来，于是同一个动词也用于征兵。

intro.en: Draft and draught are the same word in two spellings, and both go back to a verb meaning to draw or pull.
intro.cn: draft 与 draught 是同一个词的两种拼写，都可追溯到表示「拉、画」的动词。

items.en: Dragan meant to draw or pull and is the ancestor of modern draw.
items.cn: 古英语 dragan 意为「拉、拖、画」，是现代 draw 的祖先。

items.en: Draught named the act of drawing, and then the thing drawn, such as a written outline.
items.cn: draught 指「拉、画」的动作，后来指被画出的东西，例如一份文字框架。

items.en: The spelling draft became usual for written versions and for banking orders.
items.cn: 拼写 draft 逐渐固定用于文字版本与银行票据。

items.en: Military drafting developed the sense of pulling people into service.
items.cn: 军事上的征兵用法发展出「把人拉去服役」的意思。

items.en: In Britain draught is kept for air and drinks, while draft dominates in America for most senses.
items.cn: 英式英语用 draught 指气流与饮品，美式英语则在多数义项上用 draft。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the draw root or the spelling; the near-meaning group compares words for preliminary versions.
note.cn: 形近组共享「拉」的词根或拼写；近义组比较表示「初步版本」的词。

entries.definition: To make a picture with lines, or to pull something toward you.

entries.definition: A person who writes the first version of a document.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「起草人」，由 draft 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: A short plan showing main points only.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「提纲」，只列要点，比 draft 更简。

entries.definition: A quick rough drawing or description.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「速写、粗略描述」，强调快速而非完整。

entries.definition: One form of a text among several revisions.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「版本」，指多次修改中的一个形态。

normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子沿着 draw 背后的「拉」意象，以及 draft 与 draught 的分工展开。

normal.en: Dragan meant to pull, and a draft is what you pull out of your mind first.
normal.cn: dragan 意为「拉」，草稿就是你最先从脑子里拉出来的那部分。

normal.en: British air is a draught, American air is a draft, but the origin is one word.

normal.en: A bank draft pulls money out of an account on paper.
normal.cn: bank draft 是用一张纸把钱从账户里拉出来。

normal.en: To draft a soldier is to pull him out of civilian life.
normal.cn: draft 一个士兵，就是把他从平民生活中拉走。

normal.en: Redraft simply means draw the whole thing again.
normal.cn: redraft 就是「把整篇再画一遍」。

abstract.en: Picture a page covered with arrows and crossed-out lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸，满是箭头和划掉的句子。

abstract.en: Picture a curtain moving at the edge of a door.
abstract.cn: 想象门缝边轻轻摆动的窗帘。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pulling a sheet from a stack of paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从一摞纸里抽出最上面一张。

examples.en: The lawyer drafted a new contract for the deal.
examples.cn: 律师为这笔交易起草了一份新合同。

examples.en: Her second draft was much shorter than the first.
examples.cn: 她的第二稿比第一稿短得多。

examples.en: A draft blew through the open window all night.
examples.cn: 整夜都有风从敞开的窗户灌进来。

sensesIntro.en: One pulling motion produces written early versions, payment orders, air currents and conscripted soldiers.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「拉」的动作，生出文字初稿、付款指令、气流与征兵四类用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet pulled out of a stack, still covered in corrections.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一摞纸里抽出来的一页，上面满是涂改。

branches.en: TEXT: the early version and the act of making it are the noun and verb of one outline.
branches.cn: 文字线：初稿与起草动作，是同一份框架的名词与动词，即第一、五个义项。

branches.en: PLANS: budgets and agreements also begin as drawn outlines.
branches.cn: 计划线：预算与协议同样从画出的框架开始，即第二个义项。

branches.en: MONEY: a payment order is a document drawn on an account.
branches.cn: 金钱线：付款指令是从账户里画出的一纸文书，即第三个义项。

branches.en: AIR: moving air is literally pulled through a gap.
branches.cn: 气流线：流动的空气正是被从缝隙里拉进来的，即第四个义项。

senses.title: Sharp and unpleasant to taste
senses.definition: having a strong sharp taste that is not sweet
senses.definitionCN: 味道强烈尖锐、不甜的
senses.example: The medicine left a bitter taste in her mouth.
senses.exampleCN: 药在她嘴里留下了苦味。
senses.why: The word came from bite, because a bitter taste seems to bite the tongue.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自 bite，因为苦味像是在咬舌头。

senses.title: Causing deep pain
senses.definition: causing great sadness or hardship
senses.definitionCN: 带来深切悲伤或艰难的
senses.example: Losing the match was a bitter experience.
senses.exampleCN: 输掉那场比赛是一次痛苦的经历。
senses.why: A taste that hurt the tongue became a metaphor for pain in life.
senses.whyCN: 刺痛舌头的味道，被用来比喻生活中的痛苦。

senses.title: Full of resentment
senses.definition: feeling angry and unable to forgive
senses.definitionCN: 心怀愤怒、难以释怀的
senses.example: He remained bitter about the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 他对那个决定一直耿耿于怀。
senses.why: Long-held pain hardened into anger, and the same word covered it.
senses.whyCN: 长久的痛苦硬结成怒气，同一个词也承担了这层意思。

senses.title: Unpleasantly cold

senses.title: Money left after costs
senses.definition: the money that remains from income after all costs of producing or selling have been paid
senses.definitionCN: 收入在支付全部生产或销售成本后剩下的钱
senses.example: After a strong season, the bakery finally turned a profit.
senses.exampleCN: 经过一个旺季，这家面包店终于开始盈利。
senses.why: The Latin root means 'to make progress', and profit is the advance a business makes beyond what it spent.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「向前推进」，而利润就是企业在收回花费之后向前多走的那一步。

senses.title: Gain from a single sale
senses.definition: the gain made when something is sold for more than it cost
senses.definitionCN: 把某物以高于成本的价格卖出时得到的增益
senses.example: They sold the old press at a profit.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把旧印刷机卖掉，赚了一笔。
senses.why: A single transaction repeats the whole logic in miniature: buy low, sell higher, keep the difference.
senses.whyCN: 单笔交易把整套逻辑缩小重演：低价买入、高价卖出、留下差额。

senses.title: The motive to seek gain
senses.definition: the incentive to act because of the gain expected, especially in economic life
senses.definitionCN: 因预期收益而行动的驱动力，尤见于经济生活
senses.example: The profit motive drove the expansion into new markets.
senses.exampleCN: 营利动机推动企业向新市场扩张。
senses.why: Once profit is a regular result, it becomes a reason for acting, and the word names the reason.
senses.whyCN: 一旦利润成为常规结果，它就成了行动的理由，而这个词也就用来指这个理由。

senses.title: Gross profit before deductions
senses.definition: sales revenue minus the direct cost of goods, before other expenses are subtracted
senses.definitionCN: 销售收入减去商品的直接成本，尚未扣除其他费用
senses.example: Gross profit looked healthy, but rent ate most of it.
senses.exampleCN: 毛利看起来不错，但房租吃掉了大半。
senses.why: Accounts separate direct costs from overheads, so profit is split into layers and the first layer gets a qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 会计把直接成本与间接费用分开，于是利润被分层，第一层配上一个限定词。

senses.title: Net profit after all charges
senses.titleCN: 扣除全部费用后的净利润
senses.definition: the final profit after every cost, tax and charge has been subtracted
senses.definitionCN: 扣除所有成本、税款与费用之后的最终利润
senses.example: Net profit for the year was smaller than the headline figure suggested.
senses.exampleCN: 全年净利润比标题数字所显示的要少。
senses.why: The last layer is what owners actually keep, so it is marked off from the earlier, flattering layers.
senses.whyCN: 最后一层才是所有者真正留下的，因此要与前面那些更好看的层次区分开。

senses.title: Profit as a ratio of sales
senses.titleCN: 以销售额为基准的利润率
senses.definition: profit expressed as a percentage of revenue, showing how much of each sale is kept
senses.definitionCN: 以收入百分比表示的利润，显示每笔销售能留下多少
senses.example: A thin profit margin leaves little room for a price cut.
senses.exampleCN: 利润率很薄，几乎没有降价空间。
senses.why: Absolute profit cannot compare firms of different size, so it is turned into a margin, a share of each sale.
senses.whyCN: 绝对利润无法比较规模不同的企业，于是把它转成利润率，即每笔销售中的占比。

senses.title: Advantage in a broad sense
senses.definition: a benefit or advantage gained from an activity, not necessarily financial
senses.definitionCN: 从某项活动中获得的益处，未必与金钱有关
senses.example: He read the old manuals to his profit.
senses.exampleCN: 他读那些旧手册，从中获益。
senses.why: Before profit was narrowed to money, it meant any forward gain, and that older sense survives in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 在利润被收窄为金钱之前，它泛指任何前进式的获益，这一旧义仍存于正式书面语中。

senses.title: Any gain from an action
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何行动带来的净增益
senses.definition: whatever is gained from an action once its costs, including effort and risk, are counted
senses.definitionCN: 把努力与风险等代价计入后，行动所带来的任何净增益
senses.example: The expedition showed a profit in knowledge if not in money.
senses.exampleCN: 这次考察若不以金钱计，则在知识上有收益。
senses.why: Generalised, profit is simply the surplus of return over outlay, whatever the currency of each side.
senses.whyCN: 一般化之后，利润就是回报超出投入的剩余，无论两边用的是什么「货币」。

intro.en: Profit came through Old French from Latin profectus 'progress, advance', the past participle of proficere 'to accomplish', built on pro- 'forward' and facere 'to do, make'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: profit 经古法语来自拉丁语 profectus「进展、前进」，它是 proficere「完成、取得进展」的过去分词，由表「向前」的前缀与 facere「做、造」构成。年代为约数。

items.en: Facere meant 'to do, make'. Its deeper root is reconstructed, and it is the source of a very large family including effect, factory and difficult.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」。其更早词根属重构形式，它是包括 effect、factory、difficult 在内一大族词的来源。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus facere produced proficere, 'to make progress, to accomplish, to be useful'.
items.cn: 表「向前」的前缀加 facere 构成 proficere，意为「取得进展、完成、有用」。

items.en: Its past participle profectus was used as a noun for 'progress, advance, gain', the sense that passed into French.
items.cn: 其过去分词 profectus 被用作名词，指「进展、前进、增益」，这一意义传入了法语。

items.en: Old French prufit or profit meant 'advantage, gain', and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century first as a general benefit.
items.cn: 古法语 prufit 或 profit 意为「好处、增益」，英语在十四世纪借入，最初泛指益处。

items.en: The financial surplus sense hardened in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, and gross, net and margin later divided it into layers.
items.cn: 财务盈余义在十六、十七世纪逐渐固定；后来毛利、净利与利润率又把它分成几层。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact date of the financial sense is not settled, and the pre-Latin root of facere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：财务义的确切出现年代没有定论，facere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes and sound-alikes, including one that is not related at all; group two holds words for money gained, each measured at a different point.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近的词，其中有一个根本不同源；第二组都指获得的钱，但计量的位置不同。

entries.definition: A person who foretells the future, from Greek prophētēs 'one who speaks for a god'; it sounds identical to profit but shares no root.
entries.definitionCN: 指预言未来的人，来自希腊语 prophētēs「代神发言者」；与 profit 同音，却完全不同源。

entries.definition: Describes something that yields profit; it cannot replace the noun that names the gain itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述能带来利润的事物；不能取代指利润本身的名词。

entries.definition: Someone who makes excessive profit, especially in a shortage; the ending adds a tone of blame.
entries.definitionCN: 指牟取过厚利润的人，尤见于短缺时期；词尾带有谴责语气。

entries.definition: Yielding no gain; it negates the adjective rather than naming a loss.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有收益的；它否定的是形容词，而不是指亏损。

entries.definition: An increase in money or advantage; broader and less technical than profit.
entries.definitionCN: 金钱或好处的增加；比 profit 更宽泛，也不那么技术化。

entries.definition: The profit a company reports to its owners, often used interchangeably with profit in finance.
entries.definitionCN: 公司向所有者报告的利润，在金融语境中常与 profit 互用。

entries.definition: Money received from sales before any cost is deducted; profit is what survives the deduction.
entries.definitionCN: 销售中收到的钱，尚未扣除任何成本；profit 是扣除后幸存的部分。

entries.definition: The gain on an investment expressed as a proportion of what was put in.
entries.definitionCN: 投资收益按投入比例表示的增益。

entries.definition: The amount by which income exceeds outgoings, often used of public accounts rather than private firms.
entries.definitionCN: 收入超出支出的部分，常用于公共账目而非私人企业。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin steps, the real family and the real accounting phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁语演变、真实词族与真实会计搭配。

normal.en: The root means 'to make forward': profit is the step a business takes beyond its costs.
normal.cn: 词根意为「向前做成」：利润就是企业越过成本向前多走的一步。

normal.en: The family runs profit, profitable, profitability, profitably, profiteer.
normal.cn: 词族包括 profit、profitable、profitability、profitably、profiteer。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the accounts: gross profit, net profit, profit margin.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出账目层次：毛利、净利、利润率。

normal.en: The same root appears in factory and effect, both built on the verb 'to make'.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 factory 与 effect 中，二者都建立在「做」这个动词上。

normal.en: Profit is what is left; revenue is what came in.
normal.cn: 利润是留下来的；收入是进来的。

abstract.en: Picture two piles on a table, one for what was spent and one for what came back.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上两堆钱，一堆是花出去的，一堆是收回来的。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder whose lowest rung is cost and whose top rung is what the owner keeps.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，最下面一级是成本，最上面一级是所有者留下的。

abstract.en: Picture a market stall that packs up only after the till is heavier than the stock was.
abstract.cn: 想象一个摊位，只有钱箱比原先的货更沉时才收摊。

examples.en: The cooperative distributes its profit among the members.
examples.cn: 合作社把利润分配给成员。

examples.en: Rising costs squeezed the profit margin to almost nothing.
examples.cn: 成本上升把利润率压到几乎为零。

examples.en: She studied the old maps to her profit.
examples.cn: 她研读旧地图，从中获益。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不（pro）费（fit）」——成本没有白费，多出来的那部分就是利润

root: 拉丁语 profectus（进展、增益），来自 proficere（取得进展）＝pro-（向前）＋facere（做、造）；经古法语 profit 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one surplus: something comes back larger than it went out, and the word then names a single sale's gain, the motive behind it, the layered accounts of gross and net, the margin, an older sense of general benefit, and finally any surplus of return over outlay.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一份剩余展开：回流之物比付出之物更大；这个词再指单笔交易的赚头、背后的动机、毛利与净利的分层账目、利润率、较早的泛指益处，最后指任何回报超出投入的剩余。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two piles of money on a table, and the returning pile is the taller one.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上两堆钱，收回来那堆更高。

branches.en: SURPLUS: the whole business and a single sale both end with more than they began with.
branches.cn: 剩余：整个生意与单笔交易都以「比开始时多」收尾。

branches.en: MOTIVE: expected gain becomes the reason to act, and the word shifts from result to cause.
branches.cn: 动机：预期收益成为行动的理由，这个词便从结果转指原因。

branches.en: LAYERS: direct costs and overheads cut the surplus into gross and net.
branches.cn: 分层：直接成本与间接费用把剩余切成毛利与净利。

branches.en: RATIO: dividing profit by sales makes it comparable across firms.
branches.cn: 比率：把利润除以销售额，使它能在企业之间比较。

branches.en: OLD AND GENERAL: the earliest sense of any forward benefit survives in formal prose and then widens to every kind of return.
branches.cn: 旧义与泛义：最早的「任何前进式益处」存于正式书面语，继而扩展到各种回报。

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix plus a Latin verb 'to make', and the family around it keeps that same shape.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁前缀加一个意为「做」的拉丁动词构成，周围的词族也保持同样的结构。

latinIntro.en: Latin pro- and facere build proficere and its participle profectus, which French shortened into the noun English took over.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的前缀与 facere 构成 proficere 及其分词 profectus，法语将其缩短为英语接手的名词。

items.example: The prefix gives the sense of moving ahead.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀赋予「向前走」的意思。

items.example: The root is one of the busiest in English.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根是英语中最活跃的词根之一。

items.example: The verb names moving forward by doing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指靠「做」向前推进。

items.example: The participle became a noun of advance.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词变成了表示前进的名词。

items.example: The year ended with a small profit.
items.exampleCN: 这一年以小额利润收尾。
这种作物证明是有利可图的。
这片土地被以获利的方式耕作。

items.example: Profiteers raised prices during the shortage.
items.exampleCN: 短缺期间，牟利者抬高了价格。

盈利能力

牟取暴利者；哄抬牟利

definition_zh: 宣传；曝光度；公众关注；宣传材料
definition_en: the attention that a person or thing gets from the media and the public; the work of attracting such attention; material issued to promote something
core_image: 聚光灯打到舞台中央，台下无数镜头同时抬起来
scene: 新店开张前一周，街口的广告牌、手机推送和报纸角落都在说同一件事。 The little bakery got more publicity from one photograph than from a year of advertising.
sceneCN: 这里 publicity 是「媒体关注、曝光度」（第 1 个义项：来自媒体与公众的注意）；句意为这家小面包店靠一张照片得到的关注，胜过一整年的广告。图中可辨识物件：广告牌、聚光灯、镜头。

pos.zh: 宣传；曝光度；公众关注；宣传材料

derivatives.zh: public 加动词后缀 -ize，义为「宣传；推广」
public 加表人后缀 -ist，义为「公关人员；宣传员」
去掉名词后缀 -ity 得到的形容词，义为「公共的；公开的」

senses.title: Attention from the media and the public
senses.definition: the attention that a person, product or event receives from newspapers, television and the public
senses.definitionCN: 人、产品、事件从报纸、电视和公众那里获得的注意
senses.example: The court case brought the family unwanted publicity.
senses.exampleCN: 这场官司给这家人带来了他们并不想要的关注。
senses.why: Publicity is the noun form of public, so it names the state of being seen by everyone; the media only make that state visible.
senses.whyCN: publicity 是 public 的名词形式，本指「被所有人看见的状态」，媒体只是把这种状态变得看得见。

senses.title: The work of attracting public attention
senses.definition: the business or activity of persuading the public to notice a product, a person or an event
senses.definitionCN: 设法让公众注意某个产品、人物或事件的工作
senses.example: She works in publicity for a film company.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家电影公司做宣传工作。
senses.why: Once being seen has value, somebody must produce that visibility, so the noun also names the deliberate work of drawing eyes.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「被看见」有了价值，就得有人去制造这种可见度，于是这个词也指刻意把目光引过来的工作。

senses.title: Material issued to promote something
senses.definition: printed or filmed material sent out to tell the public about something
senses.definitionCN: 为向公众介绍某事而发出的印刷品或影像材料
senses.example: The hotel sent publicity to every travel agent in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店给城里每一家旅行社都寄了宣传材料。
senses.why: The work of publicity produces sheets, pictures and short films, and the same noun can stand for the things it hands out.
senses.whyCN: 宣传工作会产出文稿、图片和短片，同一个名词也就能指它发出去的那些东西。

senses.title: The condition of being open to public knowledge
senses.titleCN: 公开性；为人所知的状态
senses.definition: the state of a matter being open to public knowledge rather than kept private
senses.definitionCN: 一件事向公众知识开放、而非被私下保留的状态
senses.example: The publicity of the hearing was itself part of the punishment.
senses.exampleCN: 这场听证的公开本身就是惩罚的一部分。
senses.why: Behind the media sense sits an older legal idea that a matter belongs to the public, and the noun can still name that openness on its own.
senses.whyCN: 媒体义项背后是更早的法律观念：一件事属于公众，这个名词至今仍能单指这种公开状态。

intro.en: Publicity is public plus the noun ending -ity, modelled on a medieval Latin noun and on French publicité; its first English sense was the state of being public, and the media sense came later.
intro.cn: publicity 是 public 加名词后缀 -ity，以中世纪拉丁名词与法语 publicité 为范本；英语最早的义项是「公开的状态」，媒体义项是后来才有的。

items.en: Publicus meant belonging to the people, and from it Latin built nouns for the quality of being public.
items.cn: publicus 意为「属于人民的」，拉丁语由它造出表示「公开性质」的名词。

items.en: Medieval Latin publicitas named the quality of being public, and it is generally thought to have supplied the model for the French and English forms.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 publicitas 指「公开的性质」；一般认为这个名词为法语和英语的形式提供了范本。

items.en: French publicité widened the sense to making something known to the public, and English borrowed the word in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 publicité 把词义扩大到「使公众知晓某事」，英语在十八世纪借入这个词。

items.en: English publicity first meant the state of being public, then shifted to the business of drawing public attention as newspapers and advertising grew.
items.cn: 英语 publicity 先指「公开的状态」，随着报纸与广告的发展，转而指「吸引公众注意的行当」。

items.en: Modern English uses publicity for media attention, for the promotion industry, and for the sheets and clips that industry sends out.
items.cn: 现代英语用 publicity 指媒体关注、宣传行业，以及该行业发出的文稿与片段。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for attention and for the work of getting it.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的形式；近义组收表示「关注」以及「争取关注的工作」的名词。

entries.definition: Open to all, or the people as a whole; the adjective behind publicity.
entries.definitionCN: 向所有人开放的，或指全体民众；publicity 背后的形容词。

entries.definition: To make something widely known on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 有意让某事广为人知。

entries.definition: A person paid to keep a name in the papers.
entries.definitionCN: 受雇让某个名字持续见报的人。

entries.definition: To issue a text for the public to read.
entries.definitionCN: 把文字发行出来供公众阅读。

entries.definition: Activity that helps sell or popularize something.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助销售或推广某事物的活动。

entries.definition: The state of being seen or discussed by many people.
entries.definitionCN: 被许多人看到或谈论的状态。

entries.definition: Paid messages that persuade people to buy.
entries.definitionCN: 付费的、说服人们购买的信息。

entries.definition: Loud claims that inflate interest in something.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事物的热度吹高的说法。

normalIntro.en: The noun is the adjective public with -ity attached, and both go back to the Latin quality of being open to the people.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词是形容词 public 加上 -ity，两者都回到拉丁语「向人民开放」这一性质。

normal.en: Publicity is public with -ity, an ending that turns a quality into a noun, so it names the state of being public.
normal.cn: publicity 是 public 加 -ity，这个后缀把性质变成名词，所以它指「处于公开状态」。

normal.en: The Latin model is publicitas, a medieval noun for exactly that quality.
normal.cn: 它的拉丁范本是 publicitas，一个正指这种性质的中世纪名词。

normal.en: Publicity and publicist share a stem: one is the attention, the other is the person paid to produce it.
normal.cn: publicity 与 publicist 同词干：前者是关注，后者是受雇制造关注的人。

normal.en: Publicize is the verb, and it means to make something public on purpose.
normal.cn: publicize 是对应的动词，意为有意把某事公开。

normal.en: A publicity stunt is a planned act whose only real purpose is to be reported.
normal.cn: publicity stunt 是一种安排好的举动，唯一真正的目的就是被报道。

abstract.en: The word is a spotlight switched on: before it, a thing merely exists; after it, everyone has an opinion.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是一盏打开的聚光灯：亮之前东西只是存在，亮之后人人都有了看法。

abstract.en: Attention can be manufactured, not only received, which is why one noun covers the light and the people who aim it.
abstract.cn: 关注可以被制造，而不只是被接受，所以同一个名词既指那束光，也指操纵光的人。

abstract.en: When privacy is sold, publicity becomes a price, and the same word names the bill.
abstract.cn: 当隐私被拿去交换，曝光就成了一种价格，同一个词也用来指那张账单。

examples.en: The film got plenty of publicity before it opened.
examples.cn: 这部电影上映前就获得了大量宣传。

examples.en: He hired a firm to handle publicity for the tour.
examples.cn: 他请了一家公司为巡演做宣传。

examples.en: The case attracted publicity across the country.
examples.cn: 这起案件在全国范围内引起了关注。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「帕布利瑟提」——把东西摆到人人都看得见的灯下，就是 publicity，宣传与曝光。

root: 拉丁语 publicus（属于人民的）→ 中世纪拉丁 publicitas（公开的性质）→ 法语 publicité → 英语 publicity；由 public 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，核心是「被公众看见」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being open to the public eye; the senses divide into media attention, the work of attracting it, the material sent out, and the bare state of openness.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「暴露在公众目光之下」；义项由此分为媒体关注、争取关注的工作、发出的材料，以及纯粹的公开状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spotlight striking the middle of a stage while every camera below lifts at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：聚光灯打在舞台中央，台下所有镜头同时抬起。

branches.en: one photograph reprinted in a hundred papers
branches.cn: 一张照片被上百家报纸转载

branches.en: a name repeated until strangers recognize it
branches.cn: 一个名字被重复到陌生人也能认出

branches.en: a desk of staff ringing editors all morning
branches.cn: 一整个上午给编辑打电话的办公桌

branches.en: an envelope of glossy sheets for travel agents
branches.cn: 寄给旅行社的一叠光面宣传页

branches.en: a hearing held with the doors left open
branches.cn: 大门敞开举行的听证

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin adjective for what belongs to the people and by the English noun ending -ity, which names a quality or state.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「属于人民」的拉丁形容词和指性质、状态的名词后缀 -ity 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 指甲；趾甲；钉子；钉住；逮住
definition_en: the hard plate at the end of a finger or toe; a small metal pin used to fasten things; and, as a verb, to fix something with such a pin or to catch someone
core_image: 锤子落下，一枚小钉被送进木板，只留下一个扁平的钉帽
scene: 修鞋摊的木板上钉着一排旧鞋掌，师傅抬手示意我别碰那块松动的边角。 He drove a nail into the loose board so that it would stop rattling.
sceneCN: 这里是「钉子」（第 2 个义项：用来连接或固定木料的金属小钉）；句意是他把一枚钉子钉进松动的木板，好让它不再吱呀作响。图中可辨识物件：钉帽、旧鞋掌、木凳。

collocations.phrase: hit the nail on the head

derivatives.zh: 由 finger 与 nail 复合而成，义为「手指甲」
由 toe 与 nail 复合而成，义为「脚趾甲」
由 nail 与 brush 复合而成，义为「指甲刷」

senses.title: The hard plate at the end of a finger or toe
senses.definition: the hard, smooth layer that grows at the end of a finger or toe and protects the tip
senses.definitionCN: 手指或脚趾末端长出的坚硬平滑层，用来保护指端
senses.example: She kept her nails short so that she could work at the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 为了能在机器旁干活，她把指甲一直剪得很短。
senses.why: Old English nægl named this hard plate first; the metal pin took the same word because both are small, hard and gripping.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 nægl 最早指的就是这层硬片；金属钉后来共用同一个词，因为两者都是又小又硬、能把东西咬住的东西。

senses.title: A small metal pin used for fastening
senses.definition: a short metal spike driven into wood or a wall to join pieces or hold something in place
senses.definitionCN: 钉入木头或墙面的短金属钉，用来连接构件或把东西固定住
senses.example: The picture hung from a single nail above the door.
senses.exampleCN: 那幅画就挂在门上方的一枚钉子上。
senses.why: The Germanic word covered both the body's hard plate and the metal peg, so the shared picture is a small hard thing that holds on.
senses.whyCN: 这个日耳曼词同时指身体的硬片和金属小钉，共有的画面就是一件小而硬、能牢牢咬住的东西。

senses.title: To fasten something with a nail
senses.definition: to fix an object in place by driving a nail into it, or to attach one thing to another in this way
senses.definitionCN: 把钉子钉入某物使其固定，或以这种方式把两件东西连接起来
senses.example: They nailed boards over the broken window before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨来临前，他们用木板钉住了破掉的窗户。
senses.why: Once the noun names the tool, the verb needs no new idea: it simply names the act of putting that tool to work.
senses.whyCN: 名词既已指这件工具，动词就不需要新意思，只是把「使用这件工具」的动作说出来。

senses.title: To catch or hit exactly
senses.definition: in informal speech, to catch someone, to hit something exactly, or to do something perfectly
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示抓住某人、正好击中某物，或把事情办得无可挑剔
senses.example: The police nailed the driver at the second checkpoint.
senses.exampleCN: 警方在第二个检查站逮住了那个司机。
senses.why: A nail stops a board from moving, so the verb can picture anything pinned down beyond doubt: a suspect caught, a target hit, an answer found.
senses.whyCN: 钉子能止住木板的活动，所以这个动词可以想像任何被钉死、再无疑问的事：抓到嫌疑人、击中目标、找到答案。

intro.en: Nail is a Germanic word that has named both a hard plate on the body and a metal pin since Old English, and the two senses still share one form.
intro.cn: nail 是日耳曼语词，自古英语起就同时指身上的硬片和金属钉，这两个义项至今共用一个词形。

items.en: A reconstructed root for nail or claw is generally linked to this word, though the exact shape of the root is disputed.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词与一个表示「指甲、爪」的原始印欧语词根有关，但词根的具体形式仍有争议。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form naglaz named both the hard plate of a finger or toe and a metal peg.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式 naglaz 同时指手指或脚趾的硬片与金属钉。

items.en: Old English nægl carried both meanings, so a finger nail and a board nail were the same word from the start.
items.cn: 古英语 nægl 兼具两义，所以手指甲和木板钉从一开始就是同一个词。

items.en: Middle English kept the noun and formed the verb nailen, meaning to fasten with a nail.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了这个名词，并造出动词 nailen，意为用钉子固定。

items.en: Modern English adds the informal sense of catching someone or getting something exactly right, as in nailing a suspect or an answer.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了口语义：抓住某人或把事情做得丝毫不差，如 nail a suspect、nail an answer。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that merely sound or look close to nail; the near-meaning group collects words for claws, pins and the act of fastening.
note.cn: 形近组收只是读音或拼写接近 nail 的词；近义组收表示爪、钉以及固定动作的词。

entries.definition: A small soft creature that moves slowly with a shell on its back; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 背壳、行动缓慢的小软体动物；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The small hollow in the middle of the stomach; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 腹部中间的凹陷，即肚脐；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The back of the neck; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 后颈；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The nail on a finger, formed from finger and nail.
entries.definitionCN: 手指上的指甲，由 finger 与 nail 复合而成。

entries.definition: A sharp curved nail on the foot of a bird or animal.
entries.definitionCN: 鸟类或动物脚上弯曲而锋利的爪。

entries.definition: A short thin piece of metal used to hold things together.
entries.definitionCN: 用来把东西固定在一起的短细金属件。

entries.definition: To attach or fix something firmly in place.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物牢牢固定或连接在某处。

entries.definition: A small short nail with a wide head, used for cloth or paper.
entries.definitionCN: 钉布或纸用的、钉帽较宽的小短钉。

normalIntro.en: The word has been one shape for two jobs since Old English, and every sense grows out of something small and hard that holds.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词自古英语起就用一个词形承担两件事，每个义项都从「小而硬、能咬住」这个画面长出来。

normal.en: Old English nægl meant both finger nail and metal nail, so the two senses are twins rather than one borrowed from the other.
normal.cn: 古英语 nægl 同时指指甲和金属钉，两义是双胞胎，并非一个从另一个借来。

normal.en: Nailing a board is the verb built straight from the noun, which is why it needs no separate history.
normal.cn: 钉木板这个动词直接由名词构成，所以它没有另一段词源。

normal.en: Fingernail and toenail are compounds of finger or toe with nail, and each keeps the body sense.
normal.cn: fingernail 与 toenail 分别是 finger、toe 与 nail 的复合词，都保留了身体义。

normal.en: Hit the nail on the head pictures a hammer striking the exact spot, so the phrase means getting it exactly right.
normal.cn: 「hit the nail on the head」想像锤子正落在钉头上，所以这个说法指说得丝毫不差。

normal.en: Nail down adds down: the nail is driven fully home, so the details are fixed and no longer move.
normal.cn: nail down 加了 down：钉子被彻底钉到底，于是细节定死，不再变动。

abstract.en: A nail is a tiny thing that decides whether a heavy board stays put, which is why the word also means certainty.
abstract.cn: 钉子虽小，却决定一块重木板是否稳住，所以这个词也带有「确定」的意味。

abstract.en: Finger nail and metal nail share one word because both are a hard edge at the boundary of something softer.
abstract.cn: 指甲与铁钉共用一个词，因为两者都是较软之物边界上的一层硬边。

abstract.en: When police nail a suspect, the image is a case pinned down so that it can no longer shift.
abstract.cn: 警察 nail 住嫌疑人时，画面是一个案子被钉死，再也不能松动。

examples.en: He drove a nail into the loose board so that it would stop rattling.
examples.cn: 他把一枚钉子钉进松动的木板，好让它不再吱呀作响。

examples.en: She painted her nails a pale pink before the interview.
examples.cn: 面试前她把指甲涂成了淡粉色。

examples.en: The police nailed the driver at the second checkpoint.
examples.cn: 警方在第二个检查站逮住了那个司机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「耐哦」——钉子钉进去很耐，指甲也耐磨；记住 nail 是指甲、钉子，也是钉住。

root: 古英语 nægl（指甲；钉子），一般认为源自原始日耳曼语 naglaz，更早或与原始印欧语表示「指甲、爪」的词根有关；同族词有 fingernail、toenail、nailbrush 等。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a small hard plate or peg; the senses then divide into the body part, the metal tool, the act of using it, and the informal idea of pinning something down for certain.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一小片硬物或小钉；义项分出身体部位、金属工具、使用工具的动作，以及口语中「把某事钉死、再也无法狡辩」的意思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hammer drives a small hard pin into wood until only its flat head shows.
core.cn: 核心意象：锤子把小硬钉送进木板，最后只剩一个扁平的钉帽露在外面。

branches.en: a hand resting on a table, the tip of each finger capped in hard plate
branches.cn: 一只手搭在桌上，每个指尖都覆着一层硬片

branches.en: a row of clipped nails left on the edge of a basin
branches.cn: 脸盆边留下一排剪下的指甲

branches.en: one nail holding a heavy picture against a wall
branches.cn: 一枚钉子把沉重的画固定在墙上

branches.en: a hammer swinging down and a board going still
branches.cn: 锤子落下，木板随即不再晃动

branches.en: a case closed because the last doubt has been pinned down
branches.cn: 最后一个疑点被钉死，案子随之了结

intro.en: The entry is held together by one Old English noun, its English verb, and the compounds and endings built on it.
intro.cn: 这个词条由一个古英语名词、由它而来的英语动词，以及建在它上面的复合词与词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, and Latin has no noun that English used to build it, so no Latin cognate is listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语族，拉丁语中没有英语用来构词的对应名词，所以这里不列拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: nail of a finger or toe, metal peg
hard plate or small metal pin

definition_zh: 吸收（液体、气体、光热声）；吸收（知识、信息）；慢慢消化（消息）；消纳（成本、冲击）；缓冲（震动）；合并、吞并；使全神贯注
definition_en: to take something inward and keep it inside, whether a liquid, energy, knowledge, a cost or a person's whole attention
core_image: 一块干海绵按进水里，水从细孔钻进去，海绵一点点变沉
scene: 厨房台面上打翻了一杯牛奶，抹布往上一按，白色很快就淡了。 The sponge absorbed the spilled milk in a few seconds.
sceneCN: 这里的 absorbed 是「吸收液体」（第 1 个义项：把液体吸入材料内部）；句意为海绵几秒钟就把洒出来的牛奶吸干了。画面里有台面、抹布和那摊牛奶。

pos.zh: 吸收（液体、气体、光热、声音）；吸收（知识）；消纳（成本）；合并；使专注

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「吸收、专注」
由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「能吸收的」
由 absorbent 加名词后缀构成，义为「吸收能力」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「引人入胜的」

senses.title: To soak up a liquid or gas
senses.definition: to take a liquid, gas or other substance in through the surface and hold it inside
senses.definitionCN: 通过表面把液体、气体等物质吸进去并留在内部
senses.example: The sponge absorbed the spilled milk in a few seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 海绵几秒钟就把洒出来的牛奶吸干了。
senses.why: Latin sorbere meant to suck in, and the core image is a dry material pulling water into its holes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sorbere 意为「吸入」，核心意象是干燥的材料把水吸进自己的细孔里，所以最具体的义项就是吸水。

senses.title: To take in heat, light or sound
senses.definition: to take in energy such as heat, light or sound rather than reflecting it or letting it pass through
senses.definitionCN: 吸收热、光、声等能量，而不是把它反射出去或让它透过去
senses.example: Dark fabric absorbs more heat than a white shirt does.
senses.exampleCN: 深色布料比白衬衫吸收更多热量。
senses.why: The same inward pull is applied to energy: what hits the surface does not bounce back but stays inside it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「往里吸」的动作被用到能量上：碰到表面的东西没有弹回去，而是留在了里面。

senses.title: To take in knowledge and ideas
senses.definition: to learn and remember information, skills or ideas so that they become part of what one knows
senses.definitionCN: 学习和记住信息、技能或观念，使它们成为自己知识的一部分
senses.example: Young children absorb new sounds and words very quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 幼儿吸收新的语音和词汇非常快。
senses.why: The mind is pictured as the sponge: knowledge goes in like water, stays inside, and is slowly used.
senses.whyCN: 心智被想象成海绵：知识像水一样进去、留在里面，再慢慢被取用，因此「吸收知识」沿用同一个动作。

senses.title: To digest surprising news
senses.definition: to take in a piece of news or an experience and gradually understand what it means
senses.definitionCN: 接受一条消息或一段经历，并逐渐明白它意味着什么
senses.example: She sat by the window, quietly absorbing what the doctor had said.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐在窗边，默默消化医生刚才说的话。
senses.why: Information is first swallowed whole and only later understood, the same delay between taking water in and the material turning wet.
senses.whyCN: 信息先被整个吞下，之后才被理解；这和水被吸进去、材料随后才变湿是同一个有先后次序的过程。

senses.title: To carry a cost or loss
senses.definition: to bear an extra cost, loss or burden without collapsing and without passing it on to others
senses.definitionCN: 承担额外的成本、损失或负担，既不会垮掉，也不把它转给别人
senses.example: Large chains can absorb rising rent better than small shops.
senses.exampleCN: 大型连锁店比小店更能消纳上涨的租金。
senses.why: A cost is poured in like water; if the container is large enough it holds the whole amount, so absorb means to take the burden into oneself.
senses.whyCN: 成本像水一样被倒进来；容器够大就能全部装下，于是 absorb 从「装得下」变成「把负担收进自己这里」。

senses.title: To soften the force of a blow
senses.definition: to reduce the force of a shock, blow or sudden change so that its effect is less severe
senses.definitionCN: 减弱撞击、打击或突变的力量，使其影响不那么严重
senses.example: The thick carpet absorbed the shock of the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 厚厚的地毯缓冲了摔倒时的冲击。
senses.why: The energy of a blow is pulled into the material instead of reaching the body, which is the core image acting on force rather than on water.
senses.whyCN: 撞击的能量被材料吸走，传不到人身上；这是核心意象作用在「力」而不是「水」上的结果。

senses.title: To take over a smaller organization
senses.definition: to make a smaller company, group or area become part of a larger one
senses.definitionCN: 使较小的公司、团体或地区成为更大整体的一部分
senses.example: The small studio was absorbed into a giant media group.
senses.exampleCN: 这家小工作室被一家大型传媒集团吞并了。
senses.why: A small body is drawn inside a bigger one and loses its own outline, just as the water loses its shape inside the sponge.
senses.whyCN: 小机构被吸进更大的整体里，失去了自己的轮廓，就像水在海绵里失去形状一样。

senses.title: To hold someone's attention completely
senses.definition: to occupy someone's attention so fully that little else is noticed
senses.definitionCN: 完全占据某人的注意力，使他几乎注意不到别的事
senses.example: He was so absorbed in the game that he missed his stop.
senses.exampleCN: 他太专注于比赛，错过了下车的站。
senses.why: Attention is the last thing that gets sucked in: it is pulled entirely into one object, leaving no room outside.
senses.whyCN: 注意力是最后被吸走的东西：它被整个吸进一件事里，外面再也留不下位置，于是有了「全神贯注」。

intro.en: Absorb comes straight from Latin, and the whole family keeps the image of something being sucked inward.
intro.cn: absorb 直接来自拉丁语，整个词族都保留「被往里吸」的意象。

items.en: Sorbere meant 'to suck in, swallow'. Its deeper Indo-European origin is uncertain and usually described as reconstructed.
items.cn: sorbere 意为「吸入、吞咽」；它更早的印欧语来源不确定，通常只能写作重构形式。

items.en: The prefix ab- 'away, off' plus sorbere formed absorbere, 'to swallow up, suck in'. The force of the prefix is explained in more than one way.
items.cn: 前缀 ab-「离开」与 sorbere 合成 absorbere，意为「吞没、吸入」；关于这个前缀的具体作用，各家解释并不完全一致。

items.en: The action noun absorptio 'a swallowing up' is recorded, and it is the source of the English noun absorption.
items.cn: 动作名词 absorptio「吞没」有文献记录，它是英语名词 absorption 的来源。

items.en: The verb reached English through Middle French absorber or directly from the Latin form; the two routes are hard to separate.
items.cn: 这个动词经中古法语 absorber 进入英语，也可能直接来自拉丁语形式；两条路径不易截然分开。

items.en: The verb is recorded in the fifteenth century with the literal sense of taking in liquid; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 动词在十五世纪有记录，最初是「吸入液体」的字面义；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the Latin root sorb-; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of taking something in, each with a different limit.
note.cn: 形近组建立在拉丁词根 sorb- 上；近义组收「把东西收进来」的动词，各自的适用范围不同。

entries.definition: The noun for the process of taking something in, or for complete attention to one thing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「吸收、专注」，指吸入的过程或对一件事的完全投入。

entries.definition: An adjective for a material that can take in liquid easily.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「能吸收的」，指容易吸入液体的材料。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning so interesting that it takes up all your attention.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「引人入胜的」，指有趣到占满注意力的。

entries.definition: A frozen dessert of fruit and sugar; it has nothing to do with sucking in.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「雪葩、水果冰沙」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，与「吸入」无关。

entries.definition: To make something completely wet by leaving it in liquid for a while.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「浸泡、使湿透」，强调把东西放在液体里一段时间，比 absorb 更偏「变湿」。

entries.definition: To take in and fully integrate information, ideas or people into a larger whole.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同化、消化吸收」，语气正式，强调吸收之后融入整体。

entries.definition: To break down food, or to think about information until you understand it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「消化」，既指消化食物，也指把信息想明白，与「消化消息」一义最近。

entries.definition: To attract and hold someone's attention strongly, often by charm.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「迷住、使着迷」，只对应「全神贯注」一义，靠魅力而非好奇心。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded Latin verb and the phrases the word really appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用有文献记录的拉丁动词，以及这个词真实出现的搭配。

normal.en: sorbere is to suck in: absorb is the same pull, seen from the material's side.
normal.cn: sorbere 意为「吸入」：absorb 就是同一个「吸」的动作，从材料这一侧看过去。

normal.en: ab- plus sorbere gives the Latin verb absorbere, to swallow up.
normal.cn: ab- 加 sorbere 构成拉丁动词 absorbere，意为「吞没」。

normal.en: A sponge and a paper towel are absorbent; a raincoat is not.
normal.cn: 海绵和纸巾是 absorbent（会吸水的），雨衣则不是。

normal.en: Learn the pair absorb and absorption together: the verb and its noun.
normal.cn: 把 absorb 和 absorption 成对记：一个动词，一个名词。

normal.en: be absorbed in a book is literally being pulled inside the book.
normal.cn: be absorbed in a book 字面上就是被拉进书里去了。

abstract.en: Think of a dry cloth dropped in a puddle: the water disappears into it and the cloth grows heavy.
abstract.cn: 想象一块干布掉进水洼：水消失了，布变沉了，这就是 absorb 的画面。

abstract.en: Whatever is absorbed is not gone; it is inside, waiting to be used.
abstract.cn: 被吸收的东西并没有消失，它只是进到里面去了，等着被使用。

abstract.en: A big firm absorbs a cost the way a big container absorbs water: the level rises, but nothing spills.
abstract.cn: 大公司消纳成本，就像大容器装水：水位升高，但不会溢出来。

examples.en: This towel absorbs water much faster than the old one.
examples.cn: 这条毛巾比旧的那条吸水快得多。

examples.en: She was so absorbed in her book that she did not hear the doorbell.
examples.cn: 她看书看得太入神，没听见门铃。

examples.en: The small firm was absorbed into a much larger group last year.
examples.cn: 这家小公司去年被一个规模大得多的集团吞并了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊不吸」——嘴上说不吸，海绵一按下去，水全进去了：吸收。

root: 拉丁语 absorbere「吞没、吸入」，由 ab-「离开、向外」与 sorbere「吸、吞」构成；sorbere 更早的印欧语来源不确定，一般只写作重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses picture one inward pull: liquid, energy, knowledge, news, cost, shock, a smaller company or a person's attention is taken inside something larger.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在画同一个「往里吸」的动作：液体、能量、知识、消息、成本、冲击、较小的机构或某人的注意力，被收进一个更大的东西里面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dry sponge is pressed onto a spill and the water disappears inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：干海绵按在洒出的水上，水消失在海绵内部。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: a liquid or gas enters a solid and stays there.
branches.cn: 材料线：液体或气体进入固体并留在里面。

branches.en: THE ENERGY: heat, light and sound are taken in instead of reflected.
branches.cn: 能量线：热、光、声被收进去，而不是反射出去。

branches.en: THE MIND: knowledge is stored, and surprising news is swallowed before it is understood.
branches.cn: 心智线：知识被储存，意外的消息先被吞下、再被理解。

branches.en: THE BURDEN: a cost is carried inside and a blow has its force taken away.
branches.cn: 负担线：成本被装进内部，撞击的力量被卸掉。

branches.en: THE WHOLE: a smaller body is drawn into a larger one, and attention is drawn into one object.
branches.cn: 整体线：小机构被吸进更大的整体，注意力被吸进单一对象。

intro.en: Absorb is a Latin verb used whole in English, with ordinary suffixes building the rest of the family.

definition_en: at first or in the beginning, in an earlier state before later changes, from the place someone comes from, or in a way that is new rather than copied
core_image: 一本旧相册被翻开，第一页的照片边角发白，旁边用铅笔写着一行小字
scene: 搬家那天，旧木箱被一个个打开，最上面压着一张边角发白的照片，背面用铅笔写着几行字。 The photograph was originally taken in a village school.
sceneCN: 这里的 originally 是「起初、最初」（第 1 个义项：某件事开始的时候）；句意为这张照片起初是在一所乡村学校拍的。图中可辨识物件：旧木箱、发白的照片、铅笔字。

pos.zh: 起初；原来；原籍地；独创地
