senses.title: At the beginning of something
senses.definition: at the time when something started, before later events changed it
senses.definitionCN: 在某事刚开始的时候，其后的事件尚未改变它
senses.example: Originally, the firm had only three employees.
senses.exampleCN: 起初，这家公司只有三名员工。
senses.why: The adverb is original plus -ly, and original goes back to the Latin verb oriri, to rise, so originally points at the very moment a thing rose into being.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词是 original 加 -ly，而 original 上溯拉丁语动词 oriri（升起），所以 originally 指向一件事物刚升起的那个时刻。

senses.title: In an earlier state, before later changes
senses.definition: as something was at an earlier period, in contrast with what it has since become
senses.definitionCN: 指某物在较早时期的样子，与它后来的样子相对照
senses.example: The house was originally a small school.
senses.exampleCN: 这所房子原先是一所小学校。
senses.why: If the word marks the first moment, it can also mark the whole earlier state that the first moment led into, which is how it comes to mean what a thing used to be.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词标出最初的那一刻，它也能标出那一刻所引出的整个早期状态，于是便能表示一件东西从前是什么样子。

senses.title: From a particular place or family origin
senses.definition: used with from to name the place where a person was born or began living
senses.definitionCN: 与 from 连用，指出一个人出生或最初生活的地方
senses.example: She is originally from a town in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 她原籍是北方的一座小镇。
senses.why: A person also has a starting point, and the same adverb names that place of origin, turning the time sense into a sense of place.
senses.whyCN: 人也有自己的起点，同一个副词便用来指那个来源之地，把时间的意味转成了地点的意味。

senses.title: In a new and uncopied way
senses.definition: in a manner that shows fresh thought rather than following an existing model
senses.definitionCN: 以显出新鲜想法、而非照搬现成样板的方式
senses.example: The room was decorated originally, with colours nobody expected.
senses.exampleCN: 这间屋子的装饰很有独创性，用了没人想到的颜色。
senses.why: The adjective original also means not copied, and the adverb carries that sense into manner: to act originally is to begin something rather than repeat it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 original 也有「非复制」的意思，副词把这一层带入方式：以原创方式行事，就是开一个头，而不是重复别人。

intro.en: Originally is the adjective original with the adverb ending -ly; the adjective itself came from Latin through French, so the adverb carries the noun's idea of a starting point into the way a statement is qualified.
intro.cn: originally 是形容词 original 加上副词词尾 -ly；这个形容词本身经法语来自拉丁语，因此副词把「起点」的意思带进了句子的限定方式。

items.en: Oriri meant to rise or to come into being, and it pictured the first moment of anything that begins.
items.cn: oriri 意为升起、开始存在，描画的是任何事物开始时的第一个瞬间。

items.en: The noun origo, stem origin-, named the beginning or source from which a thing rises.
items.cn: 名词 origo 的词干为 origin-，指事物升起所自的开端或源头。

items.en: Originalis described what belongs to that beginning rather than to any later copy.
items.cn: originalis 形容属于那个开端、而不属于后来任何复制品的东西。

items.en: English joined original with -ly, the ending that turns an adjective into an adverb, and used the result for what was true at the start.
items.cn: 英语把 original 与 -ly 结合，这个词尾把形容词变成副词，并用它表示在开始时为真的事。

items.en: Modern English uses originally for the first moment, for an earlier state, for a place of origin, and for doing something in a new way.
items.cn: 现代英语让 originally 兼指最初的一刻、从前的状态、来源之地，以及以新方式做事。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem for rising and beginning; the near-meaning group collects adverbs that point to an earlier time.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语「升起、开始」词干上的词；近义组收指向更早时间的副词。

normalIntro.en: Originally is an adjective of origin wearing the adverb ending -ly, so its hooks follow the first moment of a thing rather than the thing itself.
normalIntro.cn: originally 是表示「源头」的形容词戴上了副词词尾 -ly，所以记忆钩子顺着事物的最初一刻走，而不是顺着事物本身走。

normal.en: Originally is original plus -ly, and -ly is the ending that lets an adjective describe how, when or in what way something was.
normal.cn: originally 是 original 加 -ly，而 -ly 正是让形容词去描述某事如何、何时或以何种方式发生的词尾。

normal.en: Original goes back to the Latin verb oriri, to rise, so originally almost always points at a beginning.
normal.cn: original 上溯拉丁语动词 oriri（升起），所以 originally 几乎总是指向一个开端。

normal.en: Originally from is about place, not time: it names where a person started, not when something happened.
normal.cn: originally from 说的是地点而不是时间：它指一个人从何处开始，而不是某事何时发生。

normal.en: Originally planned and originally intended both mark what someone meant before the plan changed.
normal.cn: originally planned 与 originally intended 都标出在计划改变之前某人心里的打算。

normal.en: The adverb often opens a sentence with a comma because it sets the time frame for everything that follows.
normal.cn: 这个副词常以逗号引出、放在句首，因为它为后面整句话定下时间范围。

abstract.en: A word about the first moment reminds us that every present state was once a beginning someone chose.
abstract.cn: 一个关于最初一刻的词提醒人：每一种现在的状态，都曾是某个人选择的开始。

abstract.en: Saying where someone is originally from is a way of telling a story that starts before the person can remember.
abstract.cn: 说出一个人原籍何处，就是在讲一个早于他记忆之前开始的故事。

abstract.en: To do something originally is to refuse the copy, and the adverb makes that refusal a manner rather than a thing.
abstract.cn: 以原创方式做事就是拒绝复制，而副词把这种拒绝变成一种方式，而不是一件物品。

senses.title: Happening at even intervals
senses.definition: happening again and again with the same space of time between each occurrence
senses.definitionCN: 反复发生，每次之间间隔相同
senses.example: The trains leave at regular intervals of ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 列车每十分钟一班，间隔固定。
senses.why: The Latin regula is the straight bar used for measuring: what the bar touches at even distances is regular.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 regula 是量物用的直杆：凡被杆子按相等距离量过的地方，就是 regular。

senses.title: Following the usual pattern
senses.definition: having the usual or expected form, without surprises or exceptions
senses.definitionCN: 具有通常或预期的形式，没有意外或例外
senses.example: He keeps the same regular routine every weekday.
senses.exampleCN: 他每个工作日都保持同样的常规。
senses.why: The bar rules out the crooked: the pattern is straight because it matches the rule.
senses.whyCN: 直杆排除弯曲：模式之所以「直」，是因为它合乎规则。

senses.title: Shaped by perfect symmetry
senses.definition: having all sides, angles, or parts equal or even, as a regular polygon or regular features
senses.definitionCN: 所有边、角或部分相等或均匀，如正多边形或端正的五官
senses.example: A square is the simplest regular polygon.
senses.exampleCN: 正方形是最简单的正多边形。
senses.why: Here the bar measures the shape itself: every side falls exactly on the same length.
senses.whyCN: 这里直杆量的是形状本身：每条边都恰好落在同一长度上。

senses.title: Officially proper or normal
senses.definition: belonging to the proper or official body, not temporary or unofficial, as regular troops or the regular staff
senses.definitionCN: 属于正式或官方编制，而非临时或非官方，如正规军或正式员工
senses.example: The regular army arrived to relieve the volunteers.
senses.exampleCN: 正规军赶来接替了志愿人员。
senses.why: To be on the official list is to be measured by the bar: those who pass the measure are the regulars.
senses.whyCN: 名列官方名册就是被直杆量过：量得合格者便是 regular。

senses.title: Ordinary, without special strength
senses.definition: of the normal size, strength, or kind, as a regular coffee or a regular petrol engine
senses.definitionCN: 指正常大小、浓度或类型，如普通咖啡或标准汽油发动机
senses.example: Just a regular coffee, no sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 一杯普通的咖啡，不加糖。
senses.why: The bar finds nothing over or under the line: the thing sits at the standard measure.
senses.whyCN: 直杆量出既不超标也不不足：此物恰在标准刻度上。

senses.title: A person who goes often
senses.definition: a customer, visitor, or member who attends a place often and is known there
senses.definitionCN: 经常光顾某处、为人熟知的顾客、访客或成员
senses.example: The barman sets aside a stool for his regulars.
senses.exampleCN: 酒保为常客们留着固定的凳子。
senses.why: The even intervals become habit: the person whose visits the bar could measure like clockwork.
senses.whyCN: 均匀的间隔变成习惯：这个人的到访准得像被钟摆量过。

senses.title: A soldier of the standing army
senses.definition: a member of the permanent professional army, not a reserve or volunteer
senses.definitionCN: 常备职业军队的成员，而非预备役或志愿兵
senses.example: The regulars held the bridge until reinforcements came.
senses.exampleCN: 正规军士兵坚守桥梁直到援兵到来。
senses.why: The official measure of sense four applied to a uniform: the soldier who is always on the list.
senses.whyCN: 第四义「官方名册」套到军装上：永远在编制名单上的士兵。

intro.en: Regular comes from Old French reguler, from Latin regularis, from regula 'a straight bar, a rule, a pattern', itself from regere 'to keep straight, guide'. The ruler and the ruler's bar are the same tool in two hands.
intro.cn: regular 来自古法语 reguler，上溯拉丁语 regularis，出自 regula「直杆、规则、模范」，regula 又源自 regere「保持笔直、引导」。统治者的「规矩」与木匠的「直杆」，是同一件工具握在两只手里。

items.en: The root *h3reg- 'to move straight, direct' underlies regere, and English right, reckon and rich. Straightness, correctness and wealth (the guiding hand) share one root.
items.cn: 词根 *h3reg-「直线行进、引导」是 regere 的来源；英语 right、reckon、rich 同根。笔直、正确与财富（引导之手）出自同一个根。

items.en: Regula meant a carpenter's straight edge and, by extension, any rule or pattern; regularis meant 'having the bar in it, according to rule'. Monastic regularis clergy lived under the rule of an order.
items.cn: regula 既指木匠的直尺，也引申指任何规则或范本；regularis 意为「依规而行的」。修道院的 regularis clergy 即「依会规生活的神职人员」。

items.en: Reguler passes into English in the late fourteenth century as reguler, at first of religious rule and lawful order.
items.cn: reguler 于十四世纪晚期以 reguler 的形式进入英语，最初指宗教规诫与合法秩序。

items.en: The senses spread from religion to grammar, geometry and the army: regular verbs, regular polygons, regular troops.
items.cn: 词义从宗教扩散到语法、几何与军队：规则动词、正多边形、正规部队。

items.en: The noun regular, for habitual customers and standing soldiers, grows out of the adjective in everyday speech.
items.cn: 名词 regular 指常客与常备兵，由形容词在日常语言中生长出来。

note.en: The first group gathers the regula 'straight bar' family with its negation. The second group compares the words for steady and for normal.
note.cn: 第一组汇集 regula「直杆」词族及其否定形式。第二组比较「稳定」与「正常」两类词。

entries.definition: not regular: uneven, unlawful, or off the list. The bar finds nothing straight.
entries.definitionCN: 不规则的；不定期的；非正规的。直杆量不出笔直。

entries.definition: at even intervals, again and again. It is the adjective keeping time.
entries.definitionCN: 定期地；经常地。是形容词在打拍子。

entries.definition: to keep something straight by rule, to control it. The bar applied to systems.
entries.definitionCN: 用规则管制。直杆被用在体系上。

entries.definition: an official rule, or the act of controlling. The bar written down as law.
entries.definitionCN: 规章；管制。直杆被写成法律。

entries.definition: a system of rule, of a country or a body. The bar held as reins.
entries.definitionCN: 政权；管理体制；方案。直杆被当作缰绳握着。

entries.definition: happening at fixed periods. Periodic names the clock; regular names the evenness it produces.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定周期发生。periodic 命名时钟；regular 命名它产生的均匀。

entries.definition: happening often, but not necessarily at even intervals. Frequent counts; regular measures.
entries.definitionCN: 经常发生，但间隔未必均匀。frequent 数次数；regular 量间隔。

entries.definition: as expected, usual. Normal is the statistical middle; regular is the rule that is kept.
entries.definitionCN: 如预期般的平常。normal 是统计上的中间值；regular 是被遵守的规则。

entries.definition: done by habit. Habitual is inside the person; regular is measurable from outside.
entries.definitionCN: 习惯性的。habitual 在人的内心；regular 从外部即可量得。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin regula 'a straight bar' from regere 'to keep straight', the family irregular, regularly, regulate and regulation, and the carpenter's bar that measures everything even.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 regula「直杆」（出自 regere「保持笔直」），词族 irregular、regularly、regulate、regulation，以及丈量一切「均匀」的木匠直尺。

normal.en: regula is the straight bar: whatever it measures at even distances is regular.
normal.cn: regula 是直杆：凡被它按相等距离量过的，就是 regular。

normal.en: Rule, ruler and regular all carry the same Latin bar: one is the law, one the measuring tool, one the result.
normal.cn: rule、ruler、regular 都带着同一根拉丁直杆：一个是法律，一个是量具，一个是结果。

normal.en: The prefix ir- is the Latin in- before r: irregular is simply not-measured-straight.
normal.cn: 前缀 ir- 是拉丁 in- 在 r 前的变形：irregular 就是「没量直」。

normal.en: A regular polygon has every side cut to the same length by the invisible bar.
normal.cn: 正多边形的每条边都被那把看不见的直杆裁成同一长度。

normal.en: A regular at a shop is a person whose visits the bar could have timed.
normal.cn: 商店的常客，就是到访时间仿佛被直杆量过的人。

abstract.en: Picture a metronome ticking with no drum beat to follow, perfectly even on its own.
abstract.cn: 想象一台节拍器，不跟任何鼓点，自己走得完全均匀。

abstract.en: Straightness is quiet: nothing deviates, so nothing calls attention to itself.
abstract.cn: 笔直是安静的：没有任何偏离，也就没有任何东西引人注意。

abstract.en: The bar never praises, it only approves: everything equal, everything regular.
abstract.cn: 直杆从不赞美，它只作核准：处处相等，处处规则。

examples.en: Take the medicine at regular intervals of six hours.
examples.cn: 每六小时定期服药一次。

examples.en: The garden needs regular watering through the dry weeks.
examples.cn: 干旱的几周里，花园需要定期浇水。

examples.en: Most of the tables were kept for the regulars.
examples.cn: 大多数座位都留给了常客。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞古乐」——瑞福「古」板又「乐」在其中：天天按规矩来，定时也定心 → regular 规律的；定期的；常客（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 regula「直杆；规则」（regere 引直），核心是「被直杆量过、处处均匀、合乎规矩」。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses of regular, all one bar applied again and again: to time, to shape, to the official list, to strength, and finally to the person who returns at the same hour.
sensesIntro.cn: regular 的七个义项是同一根直杆的反复应用：量时间、量形状、量官方名册、量浓度，最后量那个总在同一时刻回来的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight bar touching everything at the same, even measure.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根直杆以相同、均匀的刻度触及一切。

chain: CUT EVERY SIDE TO THE SAME LENGTH
KEEP TO THE RULE WITHOUT EXCEPTION
RETURN AT THE SAME HOUR ALWAYS

branches.en: TIME AND DEGREE: trains and coffee alike sit on the bar's standard marks.
branches.cn: 时间与浓度：列车与咖啡同样落在直杆的标准刻度上。

branches.en: PATTERN AND SHAPE: behaviour and geometry both avoid the crooked line.
branches.cn: 模式与形状：行为与几何都避开弯曲的线。

branches.en: THE OFFICIAL LIST: troops on the permanent roll are regulars in uniform.
branches.cn: 官方名册：常备编制里的军人，就是穿军装的 regular。

branches.en: THE PERSON: the even intervals settle into a familiar face at the counter.
branches.cn: 人：均匀的间隔沉淀成柜台上的一张熟面孔。

branches.en: RULE AND HABIT: what the rule demands of systems, the habit performs in a person.
branches.cn: 规则与习惯：规则对体系的要求，由习惯在个人身上完成。

intro.en: Regular adds the Latin adjective ending -aris / -ar to regula 'a straight bar, a rule', from regere 'to keep straight'. The negated ir- is the Latin in- shifting before r.
intro.cn: regular 在 regula「直杆、规则」（出自 regere「保持笔直」）上添加拉丁形容词词尾 -aris／-ar。否定前缀 ir- 是拉丁 in- 在 r 前的音变。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is regularis 'according to the regula', where regula is the carpenter's bar and, by extension, any rule. The regula bar also gives rule, ruler and regulus, the little king of the bird world.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语源头是 regularis「依 regula 而行」，regula 是木匠的直尺，引申指任何规则。regula 还给出 rule、ruler 以及戴菊莺（regulus，鸟界的「小王」）。

items.meaning: measured even; by rule; a habitual visitor
items.meaningCN: 规律的；常规的；常客（-ar 构成形容词）
items.example: He kept regular hours all his life.

items.meaningCN: 定期地；按规律地（-ly 构成副词）
不规则的；非正规的（ir- 表否定）

items.meaning: the quality of being even and steady
items.meaningCN: 规律性；均匀（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: The clock impressed him with its regularity.
items.exampleCN: 这座钟的规律令他叹服。

items.meaningCN: 管制；调节（-ate 构成动词）

items.meaning: an official rule; the act of controlling
items.meaningCN: 规章；管制（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: Safety regulations apply to all workshops.
items.exampleCN: 安全规章适用于所有车间。

items.meaning: a law of conduct; to govern
items.meaningCN: 规则；统治（经古法语 riule）

items.meaning: one who governs; the measuring bar itself
items.meaningCN: 统治者；直尺（-er 表示人或物）
items.example: Draw the line with a ruler.

items.meaning: the little king; a small bird, the goldcrest
items.meaningCN: 小王；戴菊莺（-ulus 表示小）
items.example: A regulus flitted through the pines.

items.meaningCN: 正常的（出自 norma「矩尺」，与 regular 词源不同而义近）
items.example: Nothing about the day was normal.
items.exampleCN: 这一天没有任何地方是正常的。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 依规而行的；合乎规则的

latinEntries.meaning: a straight bar; a rule, pattern
to keep straight, to guide, to rule

definition_zh: 联合；团结；使结合；合并；团结一致
definition_en: to join together so as to form a single whole or act as one
core_image: 两条河在山脚汇成一条，水色也混在一起
scene: 洪水冲垮了桥，村里几家人合起来合力搭了一座木桥。 The villagers united to rebuild the bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 unite 是「团结起来、联合」（第 1 个义项：使结合为一个整体）；句意为村民们联合起来重建桥梁。两条河汇作一条，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -ed 的形容词，义为「联合的；团结的」
同根名词，义为「团结；统一」
同根名词，义为「联合；工会」
由 unify 加后缀的名词，义为「统一；一体化」

senses.title: To join into one body
senses.definition: to come or bring together so that separate parts form one whole
senses.definitionCN: 分开的部分走到一起，形成一个整体
senses.example: The two parties united to form a single government.
senses.exampleCN: 两党联合组成了一个政府。
senses.why: The verb is the action behind union: making one out of several.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词正是 union 背后的动作：把几个变成一。

senses.title: To stand together for a purpose
senses.definition: to act together with others in support of or against something
senses.definitionCN: 为支持或反对某事而与他人共同行动
senses.example: The whole town united against the closing of the school.
senses.exampleCN: 全镇团结起来反对关闭那所学校。
senses.why: Being one body becomes being one voice, which is what the preposition against marks.
senses.whyCN: 成为一个整体，就变成了一个声音，against 正标记这一点。

senses.title: To bring qualities together in one thing
senses.definition: to combine different qualities or features in a single person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 把不同的品质或特点集于一人一物之中
senses.example: The design unites beauty with strength.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计兼具美观与坚固。
senses.why: What can be joined in the world can also be joined in a description.
senses.whyCN: 世间能合起来的，在描述里也能合起来。

senses.title: To bring people into harmony
senses.definition: to end division and bring people back into agreement
senses.definitionCN: 结束分裂，使人重新达成一致
senses.example: The loss united the family in a way nothing else could.
senses.exampleCN: 这场失去以别的方式无法做到的方式把这个家团结了起来。
senses.why: A single whole is also a peaceful one, so the verb carries the sense of harmony.
senses.whyCN: 一个整体也是一个和平的整体，因此这个动词带着和睦的意味。

senses.title: A nation under one flag
senses.definition: to bring regions into a single state or under one rule
senses.definitionCN: 把各地区合为一个国家或置于同一统治之下
senses.example: The leader united the scattered provinces into one country.
senses.exampleCN: 这位领袖把分散的诸省统一成一个国家。
senses.why: Political unity is the same joining at the scale of a country.
senses.whyCN: 政治上的统一不过是同一件事在国家尺度上的表现。

intro.en: The word comes from Latin unitus, the past participle of unire, to make one.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 unitus，即 unire（使成一体）的过去分词。

items.en: Unire meant to make one, from unus, one.
items.cn: unire 意为「使成一体」，出自 unus（一）。

items.en: The verb passed into French with the sense of coming together.
items.cn: 该动词进入法语，含「聚在一起」的意思。

items.en: English adopted unite for both joining and bringing agreement.
items.cn: 英语采用 unite，兼表结合与促成一致。

items.en: Pressure forms such as united front made it a political word.
items.cn: united front 之类的说法让它成为政治词汇。

items.en: It appears in many country names that grew from union.
items.cn: 它出现在许多由联合而来的国名里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers uni- family members, and the near-meaning group covers joining words.
note.cn: 形近组收集 uni- 词族成员，近义组覆盖表示结合的词。

entries.definition: the state of being one
entries.definitionCN: 团结；统一

entries.definition: a joining or a workers body
entries.definitionCN: 联合；工会

entries.definition: joined into one
entries.definitionCN: 联合的

entries.definition: to loosen
entries.definitionCN: 解开（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: to join two things together
entries.definitionCN: 结合；联合

entries.definition: to become one company or thing
entries.definitionCN: 合并

entries.definition: to work together
entries.definitionCN: 合作

entries.definition: to split apart
entries.definitionCN: 分开

normalIntro.en: The verb is the doing behind the noun union: turning several into one.
normalIntro.cn: 这个动词是名词 union 背后的动作：把几个变一。

normal.en: Uni- is one, and -te marks the verb of making one.
normal.cn: uni- 是「一」，-te 标记「使成一体」的动词。

normal.en: Unite against is the pattern for common enemies.
normal.cn: unite against 是面对共同敌人时的常用结构。

normal.en: United appears in the names of countries formed by joining.
normal.cn: united 出现在由联合而来的国名中。

normal.en: Unity is the state, union the body or the act, unite the deed.
normal.cn: unity 是状态，union 是实体或行为，unite 则是动作。

normal.en: Design unites beauty with strength is a common written pattern.
normal.cn: 「design unites beauty with strength」是常见的书面句型。

abstract.en: Picture two rivers meeting and running on as one.
abstract.cn: 想象两条河汇合后一起流。

abstract.en: See strangers passing buckets along a line to a fire.
abstract.cn: 看陌生人排成一列传递水桶去救火。

abstract.en: Hear a crowd break into one song.
abstract.cn: 听人群忽然唱成同一首歌。

examples.en: The workers united to demand safer conditions.
examples.cn: 工人们联合起来要求更安全的工作条件。

examples.en: Her speech united the room in a way no one expected.
examples.cn: 她的讲话以出人意料的方式让全场团结起来。

examples.en: The plan unites the old station with a modern glass hall.
examples.cn: 这个方案把老车站与现代化的玻璃大厅结合在一起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尤奈特」——尤尼是「一」，特指这一回，大家凑成一伙就是联合。

root: 拉丁语 unus（一）→ unire（使成一体）的过去分词 unitus，经古法语进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One verb covers joining bodies, standing together, blending qualities, healing division, and unifying a country.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个动词覆盖联合实体、并肩而立、融合品质、弥合分裂与统一国家。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rivers running on as one.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条河汇成一条继续流。

branches.en: The joining branch: two parties becoming one body.
branches.cn: 结合分支：两方成为一个实体。

branches.en: The action branch: standing together over a cause.
branches.cn: 行动分支：为了一个目标并肩而立。

branches.en: The blending branch: qualities held in one thing.
branches.cn: 融合分支：品质集于一身。

branches.en: The harmony branch: division ended, agreement restored.
branches.cn: 和睦分支：分裂结束，重归一致。

branches.en: The national branch: provinces brought under one rule.
branches.cn: 国家分支：诸省归于一个政权。

intro.en: A Latin root for one plus a verb ending gives the action of making one.
intro.cn: 表示「一」的拉丁词根加动词词尾，给出「使成一体」的动作。

latinIntro.en: Unire, from unus, is the Latin source; unity and union share it.
latinIntro.cn: unire 出自 unus，是拉丁语来源，unity 与 union 同出这一词根。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词后缀
items.example: Union names the act of joining.
The treaty unifies the two systems.

definition_zh: 入口；门口；进入；入场；使入迷；使出神
definition_en: a door or gate that you go through to enter a place; the act of entering; to fill someone with wonder so that they cannot think of anything else
core_image: 一扇敞开的门：人穿过它走进去，或被门里的景象牢牢吸住
scene: 暴雨中她终于找到博物馆侧面的那扇小门。 She stood at the entrance of the museum, shaking the rain off her umbrella.
sceneCN: 这里 entrance 是「入口、门口」（第 1 个义项：进入一个地方的门或通道）；句意是她站在博物馆入口处抖落伞上的雨水。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「令人着迷的」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「入迷；出神」
同源词形变化，义为「进入；条目」
同根基础词，义为「进入」

senses.title: A door or gate by which you enter a place
senses.definition: a door, gate, or passage that you go through to get into a building or place
senses.definitionCN: 进入建筑物或场地时穿过的门、大门或通道
senses.example: We waited for her at the main entrance of the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站正门口等她。
senses.why: The word comes from enter plus the noun suffix -ance, so the core image is the point where entering physically happens.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 enter（进入）加名词后缀 -ance 构成，核心意象就是「进入」动作实际发生的那扇门。

senses.title: The act of entering a place
senses.definition: the act of going into a place, or the right to do so
senses.definitionCN: 走进某个地方的行为，或获准进入的权利
senses.example: Entrance to the exhibition is free on Mondays.
senses.exampleCN: 展览入场周一免费。
senses.why: Because the suffix -ance turns an action into a noun, the word also names the act of entering itself, not just the doorway.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ance 能把动作名词化，所以 entrance 也指「进入」这个行为本身，而不仅仅是门口。

senses.title: Admission to a school or organization
senses.definition: the right or permission to join a school, university, or organization
senses.definitionCN: 加入学校、大学或组织的权利或许可
senses.example: She passed the entrance exam and entered the university.
senses.exampleCN: 她通过入学考试，进入了那所大学。
senses.why: Entering an institution is entering a gate in a figurative sense, so the act of entering extends to admission.
senses.whyCN: 进入一所学校就像穿过一扇比喻的门，「进入」的动作自然延伸为「录取、准入」。

senses.title: A person's first appearance before an audience
senses.definition: the moment when an actor or performer comes onto a stage
senses.definitionCN: 演员或表演者登上舞台的时刻
senses.example: The actor missed his entrance cue in the second act.
senses.exampleCN: 演员在第二幕错过了登场提示。
senses.why: Stepping onto a stage is entering a space in front of an audience, so the act of entering narrows to a theatrical appearance.
senses.whyCN: 走上舞台就是当着观众「进入」一个空间，「进入」于是具体化为戏剧中的登场。

senses.title: To fill someone with great wonder
senses.definition: to fill someone with delight and wonder so that they forget everything else
senses.definitionCN: 使某人充满喜悦与惊奇，以至忘掉周围的一切
senses.example: The children were entranced by the magician's tricks.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们被魔术师的戏法迷住了。
senses.why: As a verb, entrance means to make someone enter a trance-like state of wonder, shifting from doors to a spellbound mind.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时，entrance 表示让人「进入」一种入迷出神的状态，语义从门转到了被迷住的心。

senses.title: To charm so deeply that one cannot look away
senses.definition: to charm or fascinate someone completely
senses.definitionCN: 彻底迷住或吸引住某人
senses.example: The audience sat entranced throughout the whole performance.
senses.exampleCN: 整场演出中观众都看得入了神。
senses.why: This grows out of the trance image: fascination is a trance that holds the eyes and mind at the doorway of attention.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项从「出神」意象生长出来：着迷就是一种把眼睛和心牢牢拴在注意力门口的入迷状态。

senses.title: A movement inward in dance or ritual
senses.definition: a formal movement of walking into a room or ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 走进房间或仪式现场的一种正式动作
senses.example: The bride made a slow entrance as the music began.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐响起，新娘缓缓入场。
senses.why: Ceremonies turn the simple act of entering into a performed movement, extending the stage sense to formal occasions.
senses.whyCN: 仪式把「进入」这个简单动作变成一场表演，登场义由此延伸到婚礼等正式场合。

senses.title: A way in as a point of access
senses.definition: a way or means of getting access to something such as a career or a topic
senses.definitionCN: 通往事业、话题等的途径或手段
senses.example: The internship gave her an entrance into journalism.
senses.exampleCN: 这段实习为她打开了进入新闻业的大门。
senses.why: A doorway can be metaphorical, so entrance names any path that lets someone get into a field or subject.
senses.whyCN: 门可以比喻化，entrance 于是也指任何让人得以进入某个领域或话题的途径。

intro.en: Entrance as a noun comes from the verb enter plus the French-style noun suffix -ance; the verb sense meaning to fascinate was formed later from the noun, suggesting a state one enters.
intro.cn: 名词 entrance 由动词 enter 加法语式名词后缀 -ance 构成；表「使入迷」的动词用法较晚由名词引申而来，意为让人进入一种出神状态。

items.en: Latin intrare meant to go in, formed from intro (inward) and related to intra (within), the root behind English enter.
items.cn: 拉丁语 intrare 意为「进入」，由 intro（向内）构成，与 intra（在内）同族，是英语 enter 的词根来源。

items.en: Old French entrer carried the same meaning of going in, and the suffix -ance formed action nouns from verbs.
items.cn: 古法语 entrer 保留「进入」之义，后缀 -ance 则从动词构成表动作的名词。

items.en: English enter was borrowed from Old French in the Middle English period, and entrance appeared in the sixteenth century as the noun of entering.
items.cn: 英语 enter 在中古英语时期借自古法语；名词 entrance 于十六世纪出现，表示「进入」。

items.en: By the late sixteenth century entrance meant both the doorway and the act of entering, including admission to institutions.
items.cn: 十六世纪末，entrance 同时指门口与进入行为，并延伸出「入学、准入」之义。

items.en: The verb entrance meaning to put into a trance arose in the seventeenth century, generally explained as entrance (the noun) used as a verb, blending with the word trance.
items.cn: 十七世纪出现动词 entrance「使入迷」，一般认为是名词转作动词使用，并与 trance（出神）一词互相影响而成。

items.en: Today the noun stress falls on the first syllable for the doorway sense, while the fascinating verb is stressed on the second, keeping the two uses distinct.
items.cn: 今天名词「门口」义重音在第一个音节，动词「使入迷」义重音在第二个音节，两种用法靠重音区分。

note.en: Entrance has a look-alike cousin and a family of near-meaning words about doors, admission, and fascination.
note.cn: entrance 有一个形近词，以及一组关于门、准入与着迷的近义词。

entries.definition: the act of entering, or an item written in a list or record
entries.definitionCN: 进入的行为，或记录、清单中的一条；与 entrance 同根，但更常指进入行为和条目

entries.definition: a passage or area leading to an entrance
entries.definitionCN: 通向入口的过道或区域；entrance 的复合扩展词

entries.definition: a half-awake state in which you are not aware of your surroundings
entries.definitionCN: 半睡半醒、浑然不觉周围的状态；动词 entrance 与其义相关，但拼写相近且词源交织，trance 本身另为一词

entries.definition: the area just inside a door of a building
entries.definitionCN: 进门后紧挨着门的区域；与入口义近，多用于美式英语

entries.definition: the space where a door opens into a room or building
entries.definitionCN: 门洞；门口，侧重门框形成的开口本身

entries.definition: to interest someone so much that they cannot look away
entries.definitionCN: 深深吸引；使着迷，与动词 entrance 的「使入迷」义相近但更常用

normalIntro.en: Five memory hooks built on the word family and real usage of entrance.
normalIntro.cn: 五条基于词族与真实用法的记忆钩子。

normal.en: enter + -ance: the suffix turns the action of entering into the noun for the doorway itself.
normal.cn: enter + -ance：后缀把「进入」这个动作名词化，就成了「入口」这个词。

normal.en: entrance exam is the gate you must pass to enter a school.
normal.cn: entrance exam（入学考试）就是进入学校前必须穿过的那扇门。

normal.en: entrance fee: money paid at the door before you go in.
normal.cn: entrance fee（入场费）是进门之前在门口付的钱。

normal.en: make an entrance: actors enter the stage, so an entrance is also an appearance.
normal.cn: make an entrance：演员「进入」舞台，所以 entrance 也有「登场」之义。

normal.en: the verb entrance is enter + trance: it makes someone enter a trance of wonder.
normal.cn: 动词 entrance 可以拆成 enter + trance：让人「进入」一种着迷出神的状态。

abstract.en: Picture a glowing doorway that pulls people toward it like a magnet.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇发光的门，像磁铁一样把人往里吸——既是入口，也让人入迷。

abstract.en: Feel the moment you step through a gate: the boundary between outside and inside.
abstract.cn: 体会跨过大门那一刻：门就是外面与里面的分界线。

abstract.en: Imagine a viewer frozen at the theater door, unable to look away from the stage.
abstract.cn: 想象观众僵在剧场门口，眼睛再也离不开舞台——被「使入迷」的样子。

examples.en: The main entrance of the hotel faces the sea.
examples.cn: 酒店的正门面向大海。

examples.en: The audience was entranced by her violin solo.
examples.cn: 观众被她的小提琴独奏迷住了。

examples.en: His perfect score guaranteed his entrance to the top university.
examples.cn: 他的满分成绩确保了他进入那所顶尖大学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因缺死」——你因太想进去而「因缺死」在门口；进去了又被舞台迷得「因缺死」挪不开眼。谐音只是联想，与词源无关。

root: 源自拉丁语 intrare（进入），由 intro（向内）派生，与 intra（在内）同族；经古法语 entrer 进入英语，动词 enter + 名词后缀 -ance 构成 entrance；「使入迷」义一般认为由名词转类而来，并与 trance（出神）相互影响。

sensesIntro.en: From a physical doorway the word fans out to the act of entering, admission, stage appearance, and finally the verb sense of charming someone into a trance.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个具体的门出发，这个词扩展到进入行为、准入、舞台登场，最终落到动词义的「使人入迷出神」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doorway through which people or attention passes
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇门，人或注意力由此穿过

branches.en: The concrete door or gate of a building.
branches.cn: 建筑具体的门或大门。

branches.en: Entering widens into admission rights and entrance exams.
branches.cn: 进入行为扩展为准入权利与入学考试。

branches.en: Entering a stage becomes a performed appearance.
branches.cn: 进入舞台变成一场被观看的登场。

branches.en: The doorway turns metaphorical: a path into a career.
branches.cn: 门比喻化：成为进入某个行业的途径。

branches.en: Attention passes through the door of the mind into a trance.
branches.cn: 注意力穿过心灵之门，进入出神着迷的状态。

intro.en: Entrance is built from a French-learned verb plus a Latinate noun suffix, and its family shows how -ance names actions and states.
intro.cn: entrance 由一个借自古法语的动词加拉丁式名词后缀构成，其词族展示了 -ance 如何命名动作与状态。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root intr- means to go in, and it survives in a small family of English words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 intr- 意为「进入」，在英语中留下了一小族同源词。

items.meaningCN: 表动作、状态或性质的后缀
items.example: The entrance is on the left.

items.meaning: the act of entering or an item in a list
items.example: There is no entry in the log for today.
items.exampleCN: 日志里没有今天的记录。

items.meaning: money paid to go into a place
items.example: The entrance fee is ten yuan.

items.meaning: an exam for admission to a school
items.example: She is preparing for the entrance exam.
The patient received an intravenous drip.

items.meaning: a person whose attention turns inward
items.example: As an introvert, she recharges alone.
items.exampleCN: 作为内向者，她靠独处恢复精力。

items.meaning: to look inside one's own mind
items.example: He paused to introspect before answering.
items.exampleCN: 他停下来内省之后才回答。

items.meaning: to lead something in; to bring in for the first time
items.example: Let me introduce our new colleague.
items.exampleCN: 让我介绍一下我们的新同事。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加形容词后缀构成，义为「令人着迷的」
由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「入迷」
同根名词，义为「进入；条目」

definition_zh: 山峰；顶点；峰值；帽檐；达到最高点
definition_en: the pointed top of a mountain; the highest point or maximum of anything; the front edge of a cap; to reach a maximum
core_image: 一条上升的线越来越陡，最后收成一个尖，然后开始下落
scene: 登山队在最后一段岩壁上放慢脚步，前方只剩一小块尖顶。 Only a narrow peak remained above the last stretch of rock.
sceneCN: 此处指「山体最上端的尖顶」（第 1 个义项：山脊收束成的最高尖点）；句意为最后一段岩壁之上只剩一个狭窄的尖顶。图中可辨识物件：岩壁、狭窄的尖顶、登山绳、放慢脚步的队员；对应第 1 个义项。

高峰的；峰值的（作定语，如 peak hours）

憔悴的；尖耸的

senses.title: The pointed top of a mountain
senses.definition: the sharp upper end of a mountain, where its slopes meet
senses.definitionCN: 山体最上端的尖点，坡面在此交会
senses.example: Only a narrow peak remained above the last stretch of rock.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一段岩壁之上只剩一个狭窄的尖顶。
senses.why: The earliest sense is a pointed top: the word names the shape where two slopes finally meet.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项是「尖顶」：这个词命名两条坡面最终相交的那个形状。

senses.title: The highest point of a climb
senses.definition: the top that a climber reaches after ascending a mountain
senses.definitionCN: 攀登者上到山顶后所抵达的最高处
senses.example: They reached the peak just before the clouds closed in.
senses.exampleCN: 他们赶在云雾合拢之前登上了顶峰。
senses.why: A climb ends at the highest point, so the top became the goal of the whole action.
senses.whyCN: 攀登在最高点结束，于是这个顶端成了整个动作的目标。

senses.title: The high point of a career or period
senses.definition: the moment of greatest success or intensity in a process
senses.definitionCN: 一个过程中最成功或最强烈的时刻
senses.example: Her career reached its peak in the early nineties.
senses.exampleCN: 她的事业在九十年代初达到顶峰。
senses.why: A curve that rises and falls gives the metaphor: the best moment is the point where the line stops climbing.
senses.whyCN: 先升后落的曲线提供了比喻：最好的时刻就是那条线停止上升的那一点。

senses.title: A maximum value in data
senses.definition: the highest value recorded in a series, graph or measurement
senses.definitionCN: 在一组数据、图表或测量中记录到的最高值
senses.example: The graph shows a sharp peak around noon.
senses.exampleCN: 图表显示中午前后有一个陡峭的峰值。
senses.why: Statistics keeps the geometry literal: the maximum is drawn as the top of a curve.
senses.whyCN: 统计学保留了字面的几何形状：最大值被画成曲线的顶端。

senses.title: The busiest period
senses.definition: the time when traffic, demand or activity is greatest
senses.definitionCN: 交通、需求或活动最旺盛的时段
senses.example: Trains are crowded during peak hours.
senses.exampleCN: 高峰时段火车很拥挤。
senses.why: If activity is a curve, the busiest hour is where the curve peaks; the noun then names that hour.
senses.whyCN: 如果活动是一条曲线，最忙的那一小时就是曲线到达顶点之处；名词随后就指那个小时。

senses.title: The front edge of a cap
senses.definition: the projecting front part of a cap that shades the eyes
senses.definitionCN: 帽子前方突出、用来遮住眼睛的部分
senses.example: He pulled his cap down by the peak.
senses.exampleCN: 他抓住帽檐把帽子往下拉。
senses.why: A cap's brim projects forward and comes to a point, so the same shape word applies to clothing.
senses.whyCN: 帽檐向前突出并收成一个尖，同一个形状词于是也用于衣物。

senses.title: A projecting tip of anything
senses.titleCN: 任何物体的尖端或突出部
senses.definition: the pointed projecting part of a roof, beard or other object
senses.definitionCN: 屋顶、胡须或其他物体尖而突出的部分
senses.example: Rain ran off the peak of the tent.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水从帐篷的尖顶流下。
senses.why: The shape, not the mountain, is the core: any surface that rises to a point has a peak.
senses.whyCN: 核心是形状而不是山：任何升到一点的表面都有这样一个尖顶。

senses.title: To reach a maximum
senses.definition: to rise to the highest level and then stop rising
senses.definitionCN: 上升到最高水平后不再上升
senses.example: Sales peaked in December and fell sharply afterwards.
senses.exampleCN: 销量在十二月见顶，随后急剧下降。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: something peaks when it reaches the top of its own curve.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：某物到达自身曲线的顶端，就是「见顶」。

intro.en: Peak is a northern English word of uncertain Germanic origin; the mountain sense and the figurative senses developed in later centuries. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: peak 是一个来源不确定的英格兰北部词，属日耳曼语系；山的义项与比喻义是后来几个世纪发展出来的，年代均为约数。

items.en: Middle English pek, recorded in the fourteenth century, meant 'a pointed top or projecting point', not specifically a mountain.
items.cn: 中古英语 pek 见于 14 世纪，意为「尖顶或突出的尖端」，并不专指山。

items.en: The form is probably related to Old English pēac 'pinnacle' and to a reconstructed *pēc 'pointed hill'; both are uncertain and the exact link is disputed.
items.cn: 这一形式可能与古英语 pēac「尖塔、尖顶」以及重构形式 *pēc「尖山」有关；两者都不确定，具体关联仍有争议。

items.en: Similar words appear in Middle Low German and Dutch, which supports a Germanic origin, though no single source form can be pointed to with confidence.
items.cn: 中古低地德语与荷兰语中有相似词，这支持日耳曼语来源，但无法有把握地指出某一个唯一的来源形式。

items.en: The specific sense 'pointed top of a mountain' is recorded in the sixteenth century, and 'the highest point of a mountain' became standard in the eighteenth.
items.cn: 「山峰的尖顶」这一具体义项见于 16 世纪，而「山的最高点」在 18 世纪成为通行用法。

items.en: From the late eighteenth century peak was used for the highest point of anything, including careers and graphs; the transport sense 'peak hours' belongs to the twentieth century.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪晚期起，peak 用于任何事物的最高点，包括事业与图表；交通义「高峰时段」则属于 20 世纪。

items.en: Source uncertain (root and first date): the pre-Germanic origin is unknown, the Old English connection is a hypothesis, and the earliest citations are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：日耳曼语之前的来源不明，与古英语的关联只是假说，最早书证年代为约数。

note.en: The first group is made of exact or near homophones that are constantly confused in writing; the second holds words for the top of something.
note.cn: 第一组是书写中极易混淆的同音或近音词；第二组是表示「某物顶端」的词。

entries.definition: To look quickly or secretly; the spelling with double e marks the glance, not the summit.
entries.definitionCN: 快速地或偷偷地看一眼；双 e 的拼写标记「瞥一眼」，与山顶无关。

entries.definition: To annoy someone, or to stimulate interest; it comes from French piquer 'to prick', a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 激怒某人，或激起兴趣；来自法语 piquer「刺」，词根不同。

entries.definition: The past tense of the verb or an adjective meaning 'having a peak'; as an adjective it can also mean pale and ill-looking.
entries.definitionCN: 动词过去式，或表示「有尖顶的」形容词；作形容词时还可指面色苍白、有病容。

entries.definition: A bird's bill; the vowel is the same but the first consonant is /b/, not /p/.
entries.definitionCN: 鸟喙；元音相同，但首辅音是 /b/ 而非 /p/。

entries.definition: The highest point of a mountain, used especially of reaching it and of top-level meetings; it is more formal than peak.
entries.definitionCN: 山的最高点，尤用于「登顶」与首脑会议；比 peak 更正式。

entries.definition: The highest point of a shape or system, used in geometry and formal writing; it is a Latin loan and does not name a mountain by itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形状或系统的最高点，用于几何与正式写作；它是拉丁借词，本身不指山。

entries.definition: The top line of a ridge or wave rather than a single point; a crest can be long, a peak is sharp.
entries.definitionCN: 山脊或波浪的顶线，而不是一个点；crest 可以是长的，peak 是尖的。

entries.definition: The highest part of anything, in everyday speech; it lacks the sharp, pointed image that peak carries.
entries.definitionCN: 日常语中任何事物的最高部分；它没有 peak 那种尖锐的意象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real spelling contrasts with peek and pique, and the real phrases that mark the senses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：与 peek、pique 的真实拼写对比，以及标记各义项的真实搭配。

normal.en: peak (mountain) vs peek (glance) vs pique (prick of annoyance): three spellings, one sound.
normal.cn: peak（山）对 peek（瞥）对 pique（被刺恼）：三个拼写，一个读音。

normal.en: The shape is a curve: rise, top, fall — the top is the peak.
normal.cn: 形状是一条曲线：上升、到顶、下落——顶端就是 peak。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: reach the peak, peak hours, peak season, at its peak.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 reach the peak、peak hours、peak season、at its peak。

normal.en: A cap has a peak, and so does a tent; anything pointed upward qualifies.
normal.cn: 帽子有帽檐，帐篷也有尖顶；凡是向上收成尖的东西都算。

normal.en: As a verb it only means 'reach the maximum', never 'climb a mountain'.
normal.cn: 作动词时只表示「达到最大值」，从不表示「爬山」。

abstract.en: Picture a fever chart that climbs all night and turns over at dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象一张体温曲线整夜攀升，在黎明时翻转而下。

abstract.en: Picture a wave that holds its highest drop for one second before breaking.
abstract.cn: 想象一道浪在崩碎前把最高的水滴保持一秒钟。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd that fills a station at eight and is gone by nine.
abstract.cn: 想象人群在八点塞满车站，到九点又散尽。

examples.en: The peak was hidden by cloud for most of the afternoon.
examples.cn: 整个下午大部分时间，山峰都被云遮着。

examples.en: Demand for electricity peaks on the coldest evenings.
examples.cn: 最冷的傍晚用电需求达到峰值。

examples.en: Avoid the peak hours if you are driving to the airport.
examples.cn: 如果开车去机场，避开高峰时段。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「劈（pi）+ 克（k）」—— 一刀劈下去，山顶被削成一个尖 → 山峰；顶点

root: 中古英语 pek「尖顶」，可能上溯至古英语 pēac「尖塔」或重构的 *pēc「尖山」，属日耳曼语系；更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on one shape: a line rises to a single sharp top, whether that line is rock, a career, a graph, a timetable, a cap or a tent.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都立在一个形状上：一条线升到一个尖顶，无论这条线是岩石、事业、图表、时刻表、帽子还是帐篷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rising line that steepens into a point and then turns down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条上升的线越来越陡，收成一点，然后向下转折。

branches.en: SHAPE: any surface that ends in a point has a peak, from rock to canvas.
branches.cn: 形状：凡是收成一点的表面都有尖端，从岩石到帆布都算。

branches.en: GOAL: the top is what the climb aims at.
branches.cn: 目标：顶端就是攀登所指向的东西。

branches.en: CURVE: the best moment and the highest number are both the top of a line.
branches.cn: 曲线：最好的时刻与最高的数值都是某条线的顶端。

branches.en: TIME: the busiest hour is the hour when activity is at its top.
branches.cn: 时间：最忙的那一小时，就是活动到达顶端的那一小时。

branches.en: EDGE AND ACTION: a cap's brim is a forward point, and to peak is to reach the top.
branches.cn: 边缘与动作：帽檐是向前的尖，而 peak 作动词就是到达顶端。

intro.en: Peak is a bare Germanic stem with only a few English extensions; most of its family is compounds rather than suffixes.
intro.cn: peak 是一个光秃的日耳曼语词干，英语派生有限；它的词族多为复合词而非后缀派生。

latinIntro.en: No Latin etymon is recoverable: peak goes back to an uncertain Germanic form, so the Latin entry list is empty by design.
latinIntro.cn: 无法追溯到拉丁词源：peak 上溯至一个不确定的日耳曼语形式，因此拉丁条目按规则留空。

items.structure: Middle English pek, Germanic origin uncertain
items.meaning: a pointed top; the highest point
items.example: The peak is visible from the road.
items.exampleCN: 从公路上就能看见那个尖顶。

items.meaning: more than one peak; he, she or it peaks
items.meaningCN: 多个尖顶；（他、她、它）达到峰值
items.example: Two peaks rise behind the lake.

items.meaning: reached a maximum; having a peak
in the act of reaching a maximum
thin and pale in appearance, or having sharp points
items.example: He looked peaky after the long climb.
items.exampleCN: 长途攀登后他看起来面色憔悴。
非高峰时段的票更便宜。

items.meaning: the busiest hours of the day
items.example: The road is jammed in peak hours.

items.meaning: the busiest travel or sales season
items.example: Hotel prices rise in peak season.

items.meaning: the maximum demand placed on a system
items.example: The grid struggles at peak load.
items.exampleCN: 电网在峰值负荷时吃紧。
